content.thinking: Starting the multi-agent analysis: six analysts explore different angles, a checker tries to refute their claims, then three designers turn the surviving findings into ranked engine changes—all read-only and without practice sessions.

input.script:
export const meta = {
  name: 'close-the-gap-research',
  description: 'Find why suppliers stop far above C_best and design generic engine changes to capture the gap',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Analyse', detail: 'six independent analysts over the session dump, case files, cost model, docs and engine' },
    { title: 'Verify', detail: 'one adversarial checker per track tries to refute its claims' },
    { title: 'Design', detail: 'three designers with different lenses propose ranked engine changes' },
    { title: 'Plan', detail: 'merge into one ranked, testable plan' },
  ],
}

const A = args
const OUT = A.out

const CONTEXT = `
You are part of a research team helping a hackathon team (EHL Grand Finale, Tacto track) whose autonomous AI buyer agent negotiates by e-mail with supplier bots on arena.tacto.ai. The Live Final is Sun 2026-10-11 12:00 (code freeze then): ~50 hidden cases against UNSEEN suppliers, 5 themed waves of 8 minutes, one attempt per case, no human in the loop. It is now ${A.now}.

SCORE (brief/brief.md, brief/api.md): case score = clip((C_open - C_deal)/(C_open - C_best), 0, 1). C = the buyer's total cost (price, uncovered need, payment interest, freight, late delivery, quality, tooling, index clause + index risk, relationship charge for stabilise/secure_supply goals), computed by arena_kit.total_cost / cost_breakdown in ${A.root}/starter-kit/arena_kit/cost.py. C_best is "the cheaper of the best package any supplier in the case would ever accept, with every valid lever applied, and your alternative - fixed per case". The supplier's margin uses supplier_value() (payment timing at ITS cash rate, freight leg, chargebacks, tooling cash, extras; contract length and index clause are security, not cash). The rules say "Everything else counts - including weaknesses you find in our bots".

WHERE WE ARE: our final build is "A9h" (deterministic engine in ${A.root}/starter-kit/proto/: engine.py, variants.py, practice.py; Tugra's engine with config-driven tactics). Fresh full practice passes (10 hosted cases) score 0.715-0.726 mean. The practice board (best run per case): #1 NoIdea 86.9 with only ~5 rounds per case, #2 Codacabana 79.1, ..., us #10 at 74.6. Our best per case: P01 .956, P02 .684, P03 .925, P04 .874, P05 .736, P07 .710, P08 .657, P10 .679, P11 .710, P18 .532. Known records (earlier snapshot): P08 .916 (NoIdea), P05 .924 (TakeTheMoneyAndRun), P02 .847 (NoIdea), P18 .677 (NoIdea), P07 ~.81, P11 ~.81.

WHAT WE ALREADY KNOW (do not just rediscover it; build on it or overturn it with evidence):
- Our tested knobs do not move the supplier's endpoint: first ask 6% lower -> 0.672; six holds -> 0.701; a fact planner + RFQ rival loop -> 0.715. In every pass P03, P10, P11 end on the same deal (0.923 / 0.671 / 0.710); P18 always ends at EUR 5.40-5.50, P08 at 5.37-5.44.
- Yet C_best says suppliers would accept far less: P08's C_best (960,309) is about EUR 5.065/kg at pay 60, no index clause, 24-36 months (need 94,800/yr x 2-year horizon); NoIdea's P08 record implies about EUR 5.14. So the stopping point is a behaviour, not the floor - something unlocks the gap and we have not found it.
- From 1,114 supplier replies: concessions concentrate in rounds 1-2; a landed new fact + our move -> 82% concede; our own past order prices land 0/198; orders at another supplier come back "irrelevant"; a rep escalated to a pricing committee only once in 284 sessions (P02), answered with a final offer. Quality terms cost <= EUR 5k per case.
- Arena notice tonight: "If the arena's daily AI budget runs out, practice suppliers switch to a simpler rule-based brain: still online, a bit less sharp. The final is never affected." Practice quota is now 450/24 h.

DATA:
- ${A.dump}: JSON dict session_id -> full session state for ALL our sessions (309 practice, 1,263 sandbox): keys session_id, case_id, set, status, end_reason, rounds, opening, threads, result (terms, c_open, c_deal, c_alt, c_best, score, cost_breakdown, trace[] = per move {round, actor, move (our e-mail with term_sheets/refs/interpreted claims, or the supplier's offer with terms/alternatives/claim_results/status/text), reasons[] = the supplier's reasons in words, hidden figures shown as '…'}), backoffice (list of the supplier's internal notes per round: 'My call: counter/hold/final_offer/accept', etc.), listed (row with created_at epoch seconds, score).
- ${A.lb}: practice leaderboard JSON (teams, totals, rounds).
- Case files: ${A.root}/starter-kit/cases/<ID>.json (P01..P19, D01, D02; hosted practice = P01 P02 P03 P04 P05 P07 P08 P10 P11 P18; sandbox = D01 D02) with negotiable, fixed_terms, term_options, buyer rates, suppliers, alternative, round_limit.
- Data package: ${A.root}/data/ (facts.json, world.sqlite, contracts, correspondence). Team notes: ${A.root}/vault/Team-Knowledge/ (Plan/Review 2026-10-10 - worst practice cases and upgrades.md, Plan/Options 2026-10-10 - beyond tuning.md, Decisions/0007 The final build.md, Progress/). Pass logs with per-case results: ${A.root}/logs/practice-*.log; ${A.root}/logs/events.jsonl.

RULES FOR YOU:
- ${A.root} is a SHARED checkout another session is actively using. Read only: never edit, create, delete or git-anything there.
- Write your scripts and outputs ONLY under ${OUT}/<your-track>/ (create it).
- Do NOT open practice or sandbox sessions (no POST to the arena). Free GETs only if truly needed; prefer the dump.
- Never print or copy secrets (.env files).
- Python: \`cd ${A.root}/starter-kit && uv run python <script>\` imports arena_kit; plain python3 is fine for JSON work.
- Numbers must come from code you ran; cite session IDs and case IDs as evidence. Be quantitative. Solutions must be GENERIC (keyed on case features like type, category_goal, negotiable levers, supplier signals), because the final's suppliers are unseen.
`

const ANALYSIS_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    summary: { type: 'string', description: '8-15 lines: the most important things you found, with numbers' },
    findings: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'object', properties: {
      id: { type: 'string' }, claim: { type: 'string' }, evidence: { type: 'string' },
      confidence: { type: 'string', enum: ['high', 'medium', 'low'] }, score_impact: { type: 'string' } },
      required: ['id', 'claim', 'evidence', 'confidence'] } },
    hypotheses: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'object', properties: {
      id: { type: 'string' }, mechanism: { type: 'string' }, evidence_for: { type: 'string' }, evidence_against: { type: 'string' },
      test: { type: 'string' }, expected_gain: { type: 'string' }, generality: { type: 'string' } },
      required: ['id', 'mechanism', 'evidence_for', 'test'] } },
    artifacts: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
  },
  required: ['summary', 'findings', 'hypotheses'],
}

const VERIFY_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    verdicts: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'object', properties: {
      id: { type: 'string' }, verdict: { type: 'string', enum: ['confirmed', 'plausible', 'refuted', 'untestable'] },
      reason: { type: 'string' }, corrected_claim: { type: 'string' } }, required: ['id', 'verdict', 'reason'] } },
    notes: { type: 'string' },
  },
  required: ['verdicts'],
}

const DESIGN_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    candidates: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'object', properties: {
      name: { type: 'string' }, mechanism: { type: 'string' }, evidence: { type: 'string' },
      cases_affected: { type: 'string' }, expected_gain: { type: 'string' }, generality_risk: { type: 'string' },
      implementation: { type: 'string', description: 'concrete: which files/functions in starter-kit/proto, as a flagged Config field, default off' },
      test_plan: { type: 'string' }, effort_hours: { type: 'number' }, rank: { type: 'number' } },
      required: ['name', 'mechanism', 'evidence', 'implementation', 'test_plan', 'rank'] } },
    stop_the_press: { type: 'string', description: 'anything that changes how the team should test or what it should ship, or empty' },
    rationale: { type: 'string' },
  },
  required: ['candidates', 'rationale'],
}

const TRACKS = [
  { key: 'cbest', title: 'C_best anatomy', prompt: `TRACK cbest - reverse-engineer C_best per case.
For each hosted practice case (P01 P02 P03 P04 P05 P07 P08 P10 P11 P18) and sandbox D01, D02: read the case file and take c_open/c_best/c_alt from any result in the dump. Enumerate every combination of term_options for the negotiable fields (other fields at the supplier's standard / fixed values; the supplier's standard terms are in its opening offer and quote) and, per combination, solve for the unit price at which arena_kit's total cost equals C_best (C is linear in price except the relationship term - for stabilise/secure_supply cases estimate the supplier with supplier_value and note your assumptions). Then work out which combination is the actual C_best package: the arena defines C_best as the best package the supplier would accept with every valid lever applied, so model the supplier as accepting when its value (supplier_value, its cash rate estimated from its own priced alternatives in the traces, e.g. how it prices 30 vs 90 days or a clause deadband) reaches a floor; find the floor value that makes the best combination hit C_best exactly and check it is consistent across combinations. Report per case: the C_best package (terms + price), the implied supplier floor, the supplier's opening, its usual endpoint with us (from the dump), our best deal, and the gap split into (i) lever choice and (ii) price at the same terms. Also compute, for each record we know, what C and price the record implies at the C_best package's terms. Finish with generic lessons: which lever choices our deals get systematically wrong (clause, payment days, contract months, lead time, volume, incoterm, effective date), with EUR and score impact.` },
  { key: 'decision', title: 'Supplier decision rule', prompt: `TRACK decision - reconstruct the supplier bot's decision procedure from the traces' reasons and the back offices.
Mine every practice session (and the sandbox ones for contrast): the per-round supplier reasons (result.trace[].reasons) and backoffice notes. Build the vocabulary and the state machine: what the rep considers (target, band/authority, floor hints shown as '…', patience, trust, facts, our term sheets, our wording, rounds left), what makes it counter / hold / go final / agree / walk, when it escalates ('Approve a further step?') and what the committee answers. Quantify: per case and supplier, the distribution of its final price and the round it goes final; then find EVERY session where a supplier went below its usual endpoint for that case (the bottom decile) and explain precisely what preceded it (our moves, term sheets, levers, facts, wording, timing). Do the same for the rare escalations. Deliver a model of the algorithm and a ranked list of hypotheses for how to make a supplier accept a package near C_best, each with evidence for and against and a cheap test.` },
  { key: 'brain', title: 'AI vs rule-based brain', prompt: `TRACK brain - which supplier brain answered each session?
The arena notice: if its daily AI budget runs out, practice suppliers switch to a simpler rule-based brain (the final is never affected). Classify every practice session (and check sandbox) as AI-brain or rule-based, and find when switches happened (listed.created_at, epoch seconds; CEST = UTC+2). Signals to test: reply text diversity and templating (identical texts across sessions), reasons/back-office style, determinism (identical inputs -> identical outputs; identical outcomes across different inputs), how texts react to our wording, offer structure. Then map tonight's A/B passes to sessions (logs/practice-*.log names like knob-anchor6-2005, knob-holds6-2001, knob-linear-2007, knob-rfqport-1958, a9h*, a9i/a9j, a10, plan/planrfq; match by case + score + time) and say which brain each pass faced. Does the 'identical endpoints' observation come from the rule-based brain? Do any of tonight's conclusions change if we only count AI-brain sessions? If the AI brain behaves differently, characterise how (concession sizes, endpoints, reaction to facts). This matters a lot: the final runs on the AI brain only.` },
  { key: 'mechanics', title: 'Mechanics and bot weaknesses', prompt: `TRACK mechanics - every lever the buyer has and every mechanic the bots respond to, and which we leave unused.
Read brief/brief.md, brief/api.md, brief/submission.md fully; the arena FAQ (https://arena.tacto.ai/faq, use WebFetch) and the kit README (https://github.com/tacto-ai/negotiation-arena-kit) plus the local starter-kit README and the house agent (starter-kit/arena_kit/agents/llm.py prompt). List all message types and fields (term sheets, alternatives, refs/claims, attachments, signals such as reply_delay_days / validity_days, patience/timeouts, trust/contradicted, duplicates, final offers, walk-away, round_limit, RFQ rival visibility, must-haves, c_alt, letters and the Sunday 08:00 release, standard terms PDFs, 8D reports). The rules say weaknesses in the bots count. For each mechanic, check in the dump whether our engine uses it and what happened when it (or something like it) was used. Look specifically for under-used levers and plausible bot weaknesses: asking the supplier for its own alternatives/packages, proposing several term sheets at once, re-anchoring after a final offer, citing our alternative quote, deadlines, award announcements, volume or contract-length trades, effective date, tooling, chargebacks, ppm, accepting a supplier alternative, sending nothing (timeouts), tone. Output a ranked list of concrete, testable tactics with evidence and expected effect.` },
  { key: 'engine', title: 'Engine vs C_best', prompt: `TRACK engine - where does A9h leave value relative to the C_best package?
Read the engine (starter-kit/proto/engine.py, variants.py, practice.py; the A9h config in variants.py) and the traces of A9h sessions in the dump (the most recent ~100 practice sessions are mostly A9h-family). For each hosted case describe A9h's opening ask and package set (MESO term sheets), its concession path, its accept rule, which levers it offers or concedes, and contrast with the C_best package (compute it yourself with arena_kit.total_cost over the case's term_options: the cheapest package for us at the supplier's plausible floor). Does A9h ever propose the C_best lever combination? Where exactly does it leave value (clause offered, payment days, contract months, lead time, accepting a supplier alternative that is dear for us, accepting too early, not trying the supplier's alternatives)? Identify the code-level causes (function names, config fields) and minimal FLAGGED changes (new Config fields, default off) that would steer the engine toward the C_best package, generically.` },
  { key: 'contrast', title: 'Where we reach C_best vs where we stall', prompt: `TRACK contrast - why do we reach ~C_best on some cases and stall on others?
We hit 0.98 on sandbox D01 and 0.92-0.96 on P01/P03, but stall at 0.53-0.71 on P18, P08, P10, P02, P07, P11, P05. Using the dump (1,263 sandbox + 309 practice sessions) and the case files, contrast the two groups: supplier personas and signals, the case type and category_goal, the room (C_open - C_best) relative to price, what the supplier must give up to reach C_best (price % below opening, below current price, below its own cost hints), whether C_best needs a lever change vs only price, how many rounds and which moves preceded the near-C_best deals, how fast each supplier concedes per round and where it stops relative to C_best. Also use the sandbox's many sessions to test cause and effect at scale (different engines and variants played D01/D02 hundreds of times): which of our behaviours correlate with getting closer to C_best there. Deliver: the features that predict stalling, and hypotheses for what would unlock the stalled cases, with evidence.` },
]

phase('Analyse')
const results = await pipeline(
  TRACKS,
  t => agent(`${CONTEXT}\n\n${t.prompt}\n\nWrite your files under ${OUT}/${t.key}/. Return the structured result; put the key numbers in findings.`, { label: `analyse:${t.key}`, phase: 'Analyse', schema: ANALYSIS_SCHEMA }),
  (res, t) => {
    if (!res) return null
    const claims = JSON.stringify({ findings: res.findings, hypotheses: res.hypotheses }, null, 1)
    return agent(`${CONTEXT}\n\nYou are an adversarial checker for track "${t.key}" (${t.title}). Another analyst produced the findings and hypotheses below. Your job is to REFUTE them where you can: recompute every key number yourself from the dump, the case files and arena_kit (write scripts under ${OUT}/verify-${t.key}/), look for counter-examples, confounders (e.g. rule-based vs AI brain, different engine variants, cached replies, small samples, case mix), and logic errors. Default to 'plausible' rather than 'confirmed' unless you reproduced it; 'refuted' if the data contradicts it. Give a corrected claim when the direction holds but the numbers do not.\n\nCLAIMS:\n${claims}`, { label: `verify:${t.key}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERIFY_SCHEMA })
      .then(v => ({ track: t.key, title: t.title, analysis: res, verify: v }))
  },
)

const done = results.filter(Boolean)
log(`${done.length}/${TRACKS.length} tracks analysed and checked`)

const brief = done.map(r => {
  const vmap = {}
  for (const v of ((r.verify && r.verify.verdicts) || [])) vmap[v.id] = v
  const tag = id => vmap[id] ? ` [check: ${vmap[id].verdict}${vmap[id].corrected_claim ? ' -> ' + vmap[id].corrected_claim : ''}; ${vmap[id].reason}]` : ' [unchecked]'
  return `### Track ${r.track}: ${r.title}\nSUMMARY: ${r.analysis.summary}\nFINDINGS:\n` +
    r.analysis.findings.map(f => `- (${f.id}, ${f.confidence}) ${f.claim} | evidence: ${f.evidence}${f.score_impact ? ' | impact: ' + f.score_impact : ''}${tag(f.id)}`).join('\n') +
    `\nHYPOTHESES:\n` +
    r.analysis.hypotheses.map(h => `- (${h.id}) ${h.mechanism} | for: ${h.evidence_for}${h.evidence_against ? ' | against: ' + h.evidence_against : ''} | test: ${h.test}${h.expected_gain ? ' | gain: ' + h.expected_gain : ''}${h.generality ? ' | generality: ' + h.generality : ''}${tag(h.id)}`).join('\n') +
    (r.verify && r.verify.notes ? `\nCHECKER NOTES: ${r.verify.notes}` : '')
}).join('\n\n')

phase('Design')
const LENSES = [
  { key: 'gain', lens: 'MAXIMUM EXPECTED SCORE GAIN on the final: which changes capture the most of the gap between our endpoints and C_best, across case types' },
  { key: 'robust', lens: 'ROBUSTNESS ON UNSEEN SUPPLIERS: which changes are generic, keyed on case features, and cannot produce zeros (broken must-haves, no deal, timeouts, contradicted claims) on suppliers we have never met' },
  { key: 'build', lens: 'SHIPPABLE BY 06:00 WITH EVIDENCE: which changes can be built as flagged A9h variants in a few hours and validated on the free sandbox, then on a handful of practice sessions (241 left; keep ~40 for Sunday)' },
]
const designs = await parallel(LENSES.map(l => () => agent(`${CONTEXT}\n\nYou are a designer. Lens: ${l.lens}.\nBelow are six research tracks with an adversarial checker's verdicts in brackets. Trust confirmed/plausible items, discount refuted ones. Propose up to 6 candidate engine changes for A9h (each as a flagged Config field, default off, in starter-kit/proto), ranked. For each: mechanism, evidence (cite track ids), cases affected, expected gain, generality risk, concrete implementation (files, functions, config fields), and a test plan (sandbox first, then which practice cases, how many sessions, what result would accept or reject it). If the research shows the team is testing the wrong thing (e.g. rule-based brain), say so in stop_the_press.\n\nRESEARCH:\n${brief}`, { label: `design:${l.key}`, phase: 'Design', schema: DESIGN_SCHEMA })))

phase('Plan')
const designText = designs.filter(Boolean).map((d, i) => `### Designer ${LENSES[i].key}\nSTOP THE PRESS: ${d.stop_the_press || '-'}\nRATIONALE: ${d.rationale}\n` +
  d.candidates.map(c => `- [${c.rank}] ${c.name}: ${c.mechanism} | evidence: ${c.evidence} | cases: ${c.cases_affected || '-'} | gain: ${c.expected_gain || '-'} | risk: ${c.generality_risk || '-'} | impl: ${c.implementation} | test: ${c.test_plan} | hours: ${c.effort_hours ?? '-'}`).join('\n')).join('\n\n')

const plan = await agent(`${CONTEXT}\n\nYou are the lead. Merge the three designers' proposals (below) and the research into ONE plan for the next 6 hours (now ${A.now}; final at 12:00, Sunday data release 08:00, pre-flight 09:00). Output markdown with: (1) the 3-5 most important facts we learned (with numbers and the checker's verdicts), (2) stop-the-press items, (3) a ranked list of at most 5 engine changes to build as flagged variants, each with exact implementation notes (files/functions/config), the expected gain and the go/no-go test (sandbox, then practice cases and session counts), (4) what NOT to do. Be decisive and concrete; no hedging filler.\n\nRESEARCH:\n${brief}\n\nDESIGNS:\n${designText}`, { label: 'plan', phase: 'Plan' })

return { plan, designs: designs.filter(Boolean), tracks: done }

export const meta = {
  name: 'close-the-gap-research',
  description: 'Find why suppliers stop far above C_best and design generic engine changes to capture the gap',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Analyse', detail: 'six independent analysts over the session dump, case files, cost model, docs and engine' },
    { title: 'Verify', detail: 'one adversarial checker per track tries to refute its claims' },
    { title: 'Design', detail: 'three designers with different lenses propose ranked engine changes' },
    { title: 'Plan', detail: 'merge into one ranked, testable plan' },
  ],
}

const A = args
const OUT = A.out

const CONTEXT = `
You are part of a research team helping a hackathon team (EHL Grand Finale, Tacto track) whose autonomous AI buyer agent negotiates by e-mail with supplier bots on arena.tacto.ai. The Live Final is Sun 2026-10-11 12:00 (code freeze then): ~50 hidden cases against UNSEEN suppliers, 5 themed waves of 8 minutes, one attempt per case, no human in the loop. It is now ${A.now}.

SCORE (brief/brief.md, brief/api.md): case score = clip((C_open - C_deal)/(C_open - C_best), 0, 1). C = the buyer's total cost (price, uncovered need, payment interest, freight, late delivery, quality, tooling, index clause + index risk, relationship charge for stabilise/secure_supply goals), computed by arena_kit.total_cost / cost_breakdown in ${A.root}/starter-kit/arena_kit/cost.py. C_best is "the cheaper of the best package any supplier in the case would ever accept, with every valid lever applied, and your alternative - fixed per case". The supplier's margin uses supplier_value() (payment timing at ITS cash rate, freight leg, chargebacks, tooling cash, extras; contract length and index clause are security, not cash). The rules say "Everything else counts - including weaknesses you find in our bots".

WHERE WE ARE: our final build is "A9h" (deterministic engine in ${A.root}/starter-kit/proto/: engine.py, variants.py, practice.py; Tugra's engine with config-driven tactics). Fresh full practice passes (10 hosted cases) score 0.715-0.726 mean. The practice board (best run per case): #1 NoIdea 86.9 with only ~5 rounds per case, #2 Codacabana 79.1, ..., us #10 at 74.6. Our best per case: P01 .956, P02 .684, P03 .925, P04 .874, P05 .736, P07 .710, P08 .657, P10 .679, P11 .710, P18 .532. Known records (earlier snapshot): P08 .916 (NoIdea), P05 .924 (TakeTheMoneyAndRun), P02 .847 (NoIdea), P18 .677 (NoIdea), P07 ~.81, P11 ~.81.

WHAT WE ALREADY KNOW (do not just rediscover it; build on it or overturn it with evidence):
- Our tested knobs do not move the supplier's endpoint: first ask 6% lower -> 0.672; six holds -> 0.701; a fact planner + RFQ rival loop -> 0.715. In every pass P03, P10, P11 end on the same deal (0.923 / 0.671 / 0.710); P18 always ends at EUR 5.40-5.50, P08 at 5.37-5.44.
- Yet C_best says suppliers would accept far less: P08's C_best (960,309) is about EUR 5.065/kg at pay 60, no index clause, 24-36 months (need 94,800/yr x 2-year horizon); NoIdea's P08 record implies about EUR 5.14. So the stopping point is a behaviour, not the floor - something unlocks the gap and we have not found it.
- From 1,114 supplier replies: concessions concentrate in rounds 1-2; a landed new fact + our move -> 82% concede; our own past order prices land 0/198; orders at another supplier come back "irrelevant"; a rep escalated to a pricing committee only once in 284 sessions (P02), answered with a final offer. Quality terms cost <= EUR 5k per case.
- Arena notice tonight: "If the arena's daily AI budget runs out, practice suppliers switch to a simpler rule-based brain: still online, a bit less sharp. The final is never affected." Practice quota is now 450/24 h.

DATA:
- ${A.dump}: JSON dict session_id -> full session state for ALL our sessions (309 practice, 1,263 sandbox): keys session_id, case_id, set, status, end_reason, rounds, opening, threads, result (terms, c_open, c_deal, c_alt, c_best, score, cost_breakdown, trace[] = per move {round, actor, move (our e-mail with term_sheets/refs/interpreted claims, or the supplier's offer with terms/alternatives/claim_results/status/text), reasons[] = the supplier's reasons in words, hidden figures shown as '…'}), backoffice (list of the supplier's internal notes per round: 'My call: counter/hold/final_offer/accept', etc.), listed (row with created_at epoch seconds, score).
- ${A.lb}: practice leaderboard JSON (teams, totals, rounds).
- Case files: ${A.root}/starter-kit/cases/<ID>.json (P01..P19, D01, D02; hosted practice = P01 P02 P03 P04 P05 P07 P08 P10 P11 P18; sandbox = D01 D02) with negotiable, fixed_terms, term_options, buyer rates, suppliers, alternative, round_limit.
- Data package: ${A.root}/data/ (facts.json, world.sqlite, contracts, correspondence). Team notes: ${A.root}/vault/Team-Knowledge/ (Plan/Review 2026-10-10 - worst practice cases and upgrades.md, Plan/Options 2026-10-10 - beyond tuning.md, Decisions/0007 The final build.md, Progress/). Pass logs with per-case results: ${A.root}/logs/practice-*.log; ${A.root}/logs/events.jsonl.

RULES FOR YOU:
- ${A.root} is a SHARED checkout another session is actively using. Read only: never edit, create, delete or git-anything there.
- Write your scripts and outputs ONLY under ${OUT}/<your-track>/ (create it).
- Do NOT open practice or sandbox sessions (no POST to the arena). Free GETs only if truly needed; prefer the dump.
- Never print or copy secrets (.env files).
- Python: \`cd ${A.root}/starter-kit && uv run python <script>\` imports arena_kit; plain python3 is fine for JSON work.
- Numbers must come from code you ran; cite session IDs and case IDs as evidence. Be quantitative. Solutions must be GENERIC (keyed on case features like type, category_goal, negotiable levers, supplier signals), because the final's suppliers are unseen.
`

const ANALYSIS_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    summary: { type: 'string', description: '8-15 lines: the most important things you found, with numbers' },
    findings: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'object', properties: {
      id: { type: 'string' }, claim: { type: 'string' }, evidence: { type: 'string' },
      confidence: { type: 'string', enum: ['high', 'medium', 'low'] }, score_impact: { type: 'string' } },
      required: ['id', 'claim', 'evidence', 'confidence'] } },
    hypotheses: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'object', properties: {
      id: { type: 'string' }, mechanism: { type: 'string' }, evidence_for: { type: 'string' }, evidence_against: { type: 'string' },
      test: { type: 'string' }, expected_gain: { type: 'string' }, generality: { type: 'string' } },
      required: ['id', 'mechanism', 'evidence_for', 'test'] } },
    artifacts: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
  },
  required: ['summary', 'findings', 'hypotheses'],
}

const VERIFY_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    verdicts: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'object', properties: {
      id: { type: 'string' }, verdict: { type: 'string', enum: ['confirmed', 'plausible', 'refuted', 'untestable'] },
      reason: { type: 'string' }, corrected_claim: { type: 'string' } }, required: ['id', 'verdict', 'reason'] } },
    notes: { type: 'string' },
  },
  required: ['verdicts'],
}

const DESIGN_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    candidates: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'object', properties: {
      name: { type: 'string' }, mechanism: { type: 'string' }, evidence: { type: 'string' },
      cases_affected: { type: 'string' }, expected_gain: { type: 'string' }, generality_risk: { type: 'string' },
      implementation: { type: 'string', description: 'concrete: which files/functions in starter-kit/proto, as a flagged Config field, default off' },
      test_plan: { type: 'string' }, effort_hours: { type: 'number' }, rank: { type: 'number' } },
      required: ['name', 'mechanism', 'evidence', 'implementation', 'test_plan', 'rank'] } },
    stop_the_press: { type: 'string', description: 'anything that changes how the team should test or what it should ship, or empty' },
    rationale: { type: 'string' },
  },
  required: ['candidates', 'rationale'],
}

const TRACKS = [
  { key: 'cbest', title: 'C_best anatomy', prompt: `TRACK cbest - reverse-engineer C_best per case.
For each hosted practice case (P01 P02 P03 P04 P05 P07 P08 P10 P11 P18) and sandbox D01, D02: read the case file and take c_open/c_best/c_alt from any result in the dump. Enumerate every combination of term_options for the negotiable fields (other fields at the supplier's standard / fixed values; the supplier's standard terms are in its opening offer and quote) and, per combination, solve for the unit price at which arena_kit's total cost equals C_best (C is linear in price except the relationship term - for stabilise/secure_supply cases estimate the supplier with supplier_value and note your assumptions). Then work out which combination is the actual C_best package: the arena defines C_best as the best package the supplier would accept with every valid lever applied, so model the supplier as accepting when its value (supplier_value, its cash rate estimated from its own priced alternatives in the traces, e.g. how it prices 30 vs 90 days or a clause deadband) reaches a floor; find the floor value that makes the best combination hit C_best exactly and check it is consistent across combinations. Report per case: the C_best package (terms + price), the implied supplier floor, the supplier's opening, its usual endpoint with us (from the dump), our best deal, and the gap split into (i) lever choice and (ii) price at the same terms. Also compute, for each record we know, what C and price the record implies at the C_best package's terms. Finish with generic lessons: which lever choices our deals get systematically wrong (clause, payment days, contract months, lead time, volume, incoterm, effective date), with EUR and score impact.` },
  { key: 'decision', title: 'Supplier decision rule', prompt: `TRACK decision - reconstruct the supplier bot's decision procedure from the traces' reasons and the back offices.
Mine every practice session (and the sandbox ones for contrast): the per-round supplier reasons (result.trace[].reasons) and backoffice notes. Build the vocabulary and the state machine: what the rep considers (target, band/authority, floor hints shown as '…', patience, trust, facts, our term sheets, our wording, rounds left), what makes it counter / hold / go final / agree / walk, when it escalates ('Approve a further step?') and what the committee answers. Quantify: per case and supplier, the distribution of its final price and the round it goes final; then find EVERY session where a supplier went below its usual endpoint for that case (the bottom decile) and explain precisely what preceded it (our moves, term sheets, levers, facts, wording, timing). Do the same for the rare escalations. Deliver a model of the algorithm and a ranked list of hypotheses for how to make a supplier accept a package near C_best, each with evidence for and against and a cheap test.` },
  { key: 'brain', title: 'AI vs rule-based brain', prompt: `TRACK brain - which supplier brain answered each session?
The arena notice: if its daily AI budget runs out, practice suppliers switch to a simpler rule-based brain (the final is never affected). Classify every practice session (and check sandbox) as AI-brain or rule-based, and find when switches happened (listed.created_at, epoch seconds; CEST = UTC+2). Signals to test: reply text diversity and templating (identical texts across sessions), reasons/back-office style, determinism (identical inputs -> identical outputs; identical outcomes across different inputs), how texts react to our wording, offer structure. Then map tonight's A/B passes to sessions (logs/practice-*.log names like knob-anchor6-2005, knob-holds6-2001, knob-linear-2007, knob-rfqport-1958, a9h*, a9i/a9j, a10, plan/planrfq; match by case + score + time) and say which brain each pass faced. Does the 'identical endpoints' observation come from the rule-based brain? Do any of tonight's conclusions change if we only count AI-brain sessions? If the AI brain behaves differently, characterise how (concession sizes, endpoints, reaction to facts). This matters a lot: the final runs on the AI brain only.` },
  { key: 'mechanics', title: 'Mechanics and bot weaknesses', prompt: `TRACK mechanics - every lever the buyer has and every mechanic the bots respond to, and which we leave unused.
Read brief/brief.md, brief/api.md, brief/submission.md fully; the arena FAQ (https://arena.tacto.ai/faq, use WebFetch) and the kit README (https://github.com/tacto-ai/negotiation-arena-kit) plus the local starter-kit README and the house agent (starter-kit/arena_kit/agents/llm.py prompt). List all message types and fields (term sheets, alternatives, refs/claims, attachments, signals such as reply_delay_days / validity_days, patience/timeouts, trust/contradicted, duplicates, final offers, walk-away, round_limit, RFQ rival visibility, must-haves, c_alt, letters and the Sunday 08:00 release, standard terms PDFs, 8D reports). The rules say weaknesses in the bots count. For each mechanic, check in the dump whether our engine uses it and what happened when it (or something like it) was used. Look specifically for under-used levers and plausible bot weaknesses: asking the supplier for its own alternatives/packages, proposing several term sheets at once, re-anchoring after a final offer, citing our alternative quote, deadlines, award announcements, volume or contract-length trades, effective date, tooling, chargebacks, ppm, accepting a supplier alternative, sending nothing (timeouts), tone. Output a ranked list of concrete, testable tactics with evidence and expected effect.` },
  { key: 'engine', title: 'Engine vs C_best', prompt: `TRACK engine - where does A9h leave value relative to the C_best package?
Read the engine (starter-kit/proto/engine.py, variants.py, practice.py; the A9h config in variants.py) and the traces of A9h sessions in the dump (the most recent ~100 practice sessions are mostly A9h-family). For each hosted case describe A9h's opening ask and package set (MESO term sheets), its concession path, its accept rule, which levers it offers or concedes, and contrast with the C_best package (compute it yourself with arena_kit.total_cost over the case's term_options: the cheapest package for us at the supplier's plausible floor). Does A9h ever propose the C_best lever combination? Where exactly does it leave value (clause offered, payment days, contract months, lead time, accepting a supplier alternative that is dear for us, accepting too early, not trying the supplier's alternatives)? Identify the code-level causes (function names, config fields) and minimal FLAGGED changes (new Config fields, default off) that would steer the engine toward the C_best package, generically.` },
  { key: 'contrast', title: 'Where we reach C_best vs where we stall', prompt: `TRACK contrast - why do we reach ~C_best on some cases and stall on others?
We hit 0.98 on sandbox D01 and 0.92-0.96 on P01/P03, but stall at 0.53-0.71 on P18, P08, P10, P02, P07, P11, P05. Using the dump (1,263 sandbox + 309 practice sessions) and the case files, contrast the two groups: supplier personas and signals, the case type and category_goal, the room (C_open - C_best) relative to price, what the supplier must give up to reach C_best (price % below opening, below current price, below its own cost hints), whether C_best needs a lever change vs only price, how many rounds and which moves preceded the near-C_best deals, how fast each supplier concedes per round and where it stops relative to C_best. Also use the sandbox's many sessions to test cause and effect at scale (different engines and variants played D01/D02 hundreds of times): which of our behaviours correlate with getting closer to C_best there. Deliver: the features that predict stalling, and hypotheses for what would unlock the stalled cases, with evidence.` },
]

phase('Analyse')
const results = await pipeline(
  TRACKS,
  t => agent(`${CONTEXT}\n\n${t.prompt}\n\nWrite your files under ${OUT}/${t.key}/. Return the structured result; put the key numbers in findings.`, { label: `analyse:${t.key}`, phase: 'Analyse', schema: ANALYSIS_SCHEMA }),
  (res, t) => {
    if (!res) return null
    const claims = JSON.stringify({ findings: res.findings, hypotheses: res.hypotheses }, null, 1)
    return agent(`${CONTEXT}\n\nYou are an adversarial checker for track "${t.key}" (${t.title}). Another analyst produced the findings and hypotheses below. Your job is to REFUTE them where you can: recompute every key number yourself from the dump, the case files and arena_kit (write scripts under ${OUT}/verify-${t.key}/), look for counter-examples, confounders (e.g. rule-based vs AI brain, different engine variants, cached replies, small samples, case mix), and logic errors. Default to 'plausible' rather than 'confirmed' unless you reproduced it; 'refuted' if the data contradicts it. Give a corrected claim when the direction holds but the numbers do not.\n\nCLAIMS:\n${claims}`, { label: `verify:${t.key}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERIFY_SCHEMA })
      .then(v => ({ track: t.key, title: t.title, analysis: res, verify: v }))
  },
)

const done = results.filter(Boolean)
log(`${done.length}/${TRACKS.length} tracks analysed and checked`)

const brief = done.map(r => {
  const vmap = {}
  for (const v of ((r.verify && r.verify.verdicts) || [])) vmap[v.id] = v
  const tag = id => vmap[id] ? ` [check: ${vmap[id].verdict}${vmap[id].corrected_claim ? ' -> ' + vmap[id].corrected_claim : ''}; ${vmap[id].reason}]` : ' [unchecked]'
  return `### Track ${r.track}: ${r.title}\nSUMMARY: ${r.analysis.summary}\nFINDINGS:\n` +
    r.analysis.findings.map(f => `- (${f.id}, ${f.confidence}) ${f.claim} | evidence: ${f.evidence}${f.score_impact ? ' | impact: ' + f.score_impact : ''}${tag(f.id)}`).join('\n') +
    `\nHYPOTHESES:\n` +
    r.analysis.hypotheses.map(h => `- (${h.id}) ${h.mechanism} | for: ${h.evidence_for}${h.evidence_against ? ' | against: ' + h.evidence_against : ''} | test: ${h.test}${h.expected_gain ? ' | gain: ' + h.expected_gain : ''}${h.generality ? ' | generality: ' + h.generality : ''}${tag(h.id)}`).join('\n') +
    (r.verify && r.verify.notes ? `\nCHECKER NOTES: ${r.verify.notes}` : '')
}).join('\n\n')

phase('Design')
const LENSES = [
  { key: 'gain', lens: 'MAXIMUM EXPECTED SCORE GAIN on the final: which changes capture the most of the gap between our endpoints and C_best, across case types' },
  { key: 'robust', lens: 'ROBUSTNESS ON UNSEEN SUPPLIERS: which changes are generic, keyed on case features, and cannot produce zeros (broken must-haves, no deal, timeouts, contradicted claims) on suppliers we have never met' },
  { key: 'build', lens: 'SHIPPABLE BY 06:00 WITH EVIDENCE: which changes can be built as flagged A9h variants in a few hours and validated on the free sandbox, then on a handful of practice sessions (241 left; keep ~40 for Sunday)' },
]
const designs = await parallel(LENSES.map(l => () => agent(`${CONTEXT}\n\nYou are a designer. Lens: ${l.lens}.\nBelow are six research tracks with an adversarial checker's verdicts in brackets. Trust confirmed/plausible items, discount refuted ones. Propose up to 6 candidate engine changes for A9h (each as a flagged Config field, default off, in starter-kit/proto), ranked. For each: mechanism, evidence (cite track ids), cases affected, expected gain, generality risk, concrete implementation (files, functions, config fields), and a test plan (sandbox first, then which practice cases, how many sessions, what result would accept or reject it). If the research shows the team is testing the wrong thing (e.g. rule-based brain), say so in stop_the_press.\n\nRESEARCH:\n${brief}`, { label: `design:${l.key}`, phase: 'Design', schema: DESIGN_SCHEMA })))

phase('Plan')
const designText = designs.filter(Boolean).map((d, i) => `### Designer ${LENSES[i].key}\nSTOP THE PRESS: ${d.stop_the_press || '-'}\nRATIONALE: ${d.rationale}\n` +
  d.candidates.map(c => `- [${c.rank}] ${c.name}: ${c.mechanism} | evidence: ${c.evidence} | cases: ${c.cases_affected || '-'} | gain: ${c.expected_gain || '-'} | risk: ${c.generality_risk || '-'} | impl: ${c.implementation} | test: ${c.test_plan} | hours: ${c.effort_hours ?? '-'}`).join('\n')).join('\n\n')

const plan = await agent(`${CONTEXT}\n\nYou are the lead. Merge the three designers' proposals (below) and the research into ONE plan for the next 6 hours (now ${A.now}; final at 12:00, Sunday data release 08:00, pre-flight 09:00). Output markdown with: (1) the 3-5 most important facts we learned (with numbers and the checker's verdicts), (2) stop-the-press items, (3) a ranked list of at most 5 engine changes to build as flagged variants, each with exact implementation notes (files/functions/config), the expected gain and the go/no-go test (sandbox, then practice cases and session counts), (4) what NOT to do. Be decisive and concrete; no hedging filler.\n\nRESEARCH:\n${brief}\n\nDESIGNS:\n${designText}`, { label: 'plan', phase: 'Plan' })

return { plan, designs: designs.filter(Boolean), tracks: done }

content.text:
Everything is in motion. Here's where things stand:

**Running now:** a multi-agent analysis over all 1,572 of our sessions, including every supplier's stated reasons, the case files, the cost model, the docs and our engine. Six analysts each take one angle:
- the best possible deal per case: which terms and what price;
- the supplier's decision rules;
- whether tonight's practice replies came from the arena's simpler fallback brain;
- tactics and bot weaknesses we haven't used;
- where our engine leaves value;
- why we reach the best deal on some cases and stall on others.

A checker then tries to refute each analyst's claims, and three designers turn what survives into ranked engine changes. Nothing is edited in the shared checkout, and no practice sessions are used.

**Two leads driving it:**
1. **The suppliers' true floor is far below where they stop with us.** The best deal the arena says P08's supplier would ever accept works out to about €5.07/kg. NoIdea's record implies about €5.14; we always end at €5.37–5.44. So some behaviour is stopping the supplier early, and someone has found how to get past it.
2. **The fallback brain.** If tonight's practice suppliers were the arena's rule-based fallback, our A/B tests measured the wrong opponent. That would explain the identical endpoints and why the e-mail wording never mattered. The final always uses the AI brain.

**Collaboration:**
- MAIN has the plan and is already building one idea as a switched-off variant: on P02, the clause package goes out at its cheapest payment term, worth about +0.05–0.10 on that case.
- I've set up a separate worktree (branch `gap`, from `arda`) to build new variants without touching MAIN's checkout or the final build's defaults.

**Board:** NoIdea leads at 86.9 with only about 5 rounds per case; places 2–11 sit between 79.1 and 73.6, and we're 10th at 74.6. 241 practice sessions are left until 13:28 Sunday.

The analysis takes roughly 30–40 minutes. I'll come back with the ranked plan and start building.

MAIN confirmed the practice suppliers were on the AI brain all evening. Replies took a median of 19–38 seconds and ran 120–180 words, which is AI-written, so tonight's tests were valid. The fixed stopping points are real AI-brain behaviour, though each round's decision may still come from rules.

**One risk you should act on:** someone on another machine used our API key from 22:22 to at least 23:04.
- They ran bursts of up to about 11 sandbox sessions at once on D01 and D02, many ending in walk-aways or timeouts.
- That hit the key's limit of 10 open sessions and blocked 2 of MAIN's practice sessions.
- Neither MAIN nor I ran them, so it's probably a teammate's experiment.
- In the final, the same collision could block our cases and score zeros. Please ask the team to keep off the key during the 09:00 pre-flight and the final.

**MAIN's leads, now folded into the plan:**
- **Internal approval exists, per supplier.**
  - In P05, Dralveck said "We need to clarify this internally" in 28 of 34 sessions, then came back about 6 % lower.
  - The trigger was an ask 12–25 % below its opening plus a rival quote the arena verified.
  - Our asks drift to within 1–2 % of the supplier's offer by round 3, so we rarely give it a reason to go above its band.
- **Werdenfels (P18) states its condition:** a price below its final needs a volume commitment. Volume is fixed in that case, and 36 months, the only volume-like lever, has never been tried as a single firm offer.
- **Donautal (P08) contradicts itself:** it claims the AS-14404 index rise as cost pressure while saying its own AS-14404 is covered at fixed prices until March 2027. We've never used that against it.
- **P02:** MAIN is building the 90-day copper-clause package as a switched-off variant, worth about +0.08 on that case by the arena's formula.

**Division of work:**
- MAIN builds and validates variants on `arda` and never changes the defaults.
- I take the supplier's decision rules, with MAIN's approval lead checked first, and build in my own worktree.
- We each stay at 4 or fewer concurrent sessions, and trust a test only if its median reply time is at least 5 seconds.

The analysis is still running. When it lands I'll send MAIN the approval triggers and start building.

class Config:
    e: float = 1.0  # concession curve exponent: <1 firm until late, 1 linear, >1 concede early
    T: int = 4  # rounds over which our goal travels from the target to the reference offer
    toward: str = "standing"  # curve end: "standing" (best standing offer) or "open" (best opening quote)
    anchor: float = 0.0  # first goal = target x (1 + anchor); negative = more aggressive
    holds: int = 1  # extra rounds at an unchanged goal while the supplier still gives > hold_gave
    hold_gave: float = 0.01  # share of C the supplier must have given last round to earn a hold
    push: str = "all"  # after a final offer: "all", "rfq" (only with a fallback offer) or "off"
    pushes: int = 1  # how many small asks after a final offer
    push_pct: float = 0.015  # size of each ask below its standing price
    meso_n: int = 3  # term sheets per message (1-3)
    pick: str = "diverse"  # which packages: "diverse" or "near" (closest to the supplier's own levers)
    facts: int = 1  # new citable facts per message
    rival: bool = True  # RFQ: tell each supplier the rival's standing offer (ID + attachment)
    calc: bool = True  # attach our calculation from the supplier's own breakdown when asked
    volume: bool = True  # answer "which volume can you commit to?"
    tone: str = "warm"  # "warm" or "brief"
    max_rounds: int = 8
    # ideas from the teammates' practice runs (Team-Knowledge, 2026-10-10)
    anchor_mode: str = "target"  # "target": open at our C_target; "opening": per-goal % below the opening quote
    long_contract: bool = False  # longest contract_months >= horizon in every sheet (free for us, valued by suppliers)
    say_fixed: bool = False  # when a supplier asks for a fixed term, say it is fixed in this enquiry
    rfq_bar: bool = False  # RFQ: an early "agreed" is the bar for one more rival round, not the deal
    rfq_hold: bool = False  # RFQ: a short no-sheet e-mail keeps a final-offer supplier's clock alive
    news: bool = False  # cite news rows about the supplier (practice/final data only)
    # fixes from practice run A (Progress/Practice-Run-A-Findings)
    bottleneck_anchor: float = 0.0  # secure_supply: first ask at least opening x (1 - this); 0 = off
    meet_fields: bool = False  # one package takes the supplier's value for a term it set (e.g. its index clause)
    # from the friend's D02 replay e843da929222686e (0.661)
    rfq_stagger: bool = False  # RFQ: open with the cheapest quote first, then the others citing its fresh reply
    breakdown_arg: bool = False  # quote the supplier's own cost breakdown back (material + labour + conversion)
    volume_framing: bool = False  # monthly baseline, "quote the trade-off for a larger lot", no-overtime lead time
    # fixes from A3 on practice (E21)
    meet_insist: bool = False  # meet a term at its FIRST explicit insistence ("mandatory", "essential", ...)
    penalty_aversion: float = 0.0  # extra weight on chargebacks when ranking packages for the supplier (P11)
    never_walk: bool = False  # no alternative: counter at its price with the must-haves restored instead of walking
    meet_band: float = 0.0  # a met (insisted) term is priced at most this far below the supplier's price; 0 = off
    # fixes from A5 on practice (Progress/Practice-Run-A5-Findings)
    recall_best: bool = False  # if its offers got worse after our move, propose its best earlier package back
    proof: bool = False  # when asked for data/proof, attach a data sheet with the facts we cited
    target_prior: bool = False  # leverage/routine/quality: first ask at least a typical room below the opening (P07)
    price_freeze: bool = False  # "prices are frozen, talk about terms": keep its price, trade terms only (P03)
    # RFQ-only overrides (None = same as above): tune multi-supplier play without touching single-supplier cases
    rfq_e: float | None = None
    rfq_T: int | None = None
    rfq_anchor: float | None = None
    rfq_holds: int | None = None
    rfq_pushes: int | None = None

- **Analysis:** the six-analyst run started at 23:20 and is still going. When it finishes, I'll send MAIN what triggers a supplier's internal approval and start building.

- **Ready to test:** my worktree can run any variant on chosen practice cases at up to 4 sessions at once, e.g. P08 and P18 only. Each test is a switched-off variant, so the final build's defaults stay untouched.

"""Probe a hypothesis about a supplier with ONE session: the kit's LLM buyer (agents/llm.py) plus a strategy written
in words. Code still guards the numbers (term sheets snapped to the case's options, unknown data IDs dropped, no
accept that breaks a must-have or loses to the alternative). Not a final agent: a research tool.

    PYTHONPATH=. uv run python proto/probe.py case:P08 strategy.txt --practice [--model claude-opus-5-5] [--effort medium]

Prints the result and the replay path; writes the full session state to logs/probe-<case>-<sid>.json.
"""

import argparse
import json
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from arena_kit import ArenaClient
from arena_kit.cli import load_env

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
load_env(ROOT / "starter-kit" / ".env")
load_env(ROOT / ".env")


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("case_id")
    ap.add_argument("strategy", help="text file: the strategy for this probe, in words")
    ap.add_argument("--practice", action="store_true", help="required for practice cases (spends one session)")
    ap.add_argument("--model", default="claude-opus-5-5")
    ap.add_argument("--effort", default="medium")
    ap.add_argument("--data", default=str(ROOT / "starter-kit" / "data" / "package"))
    a = ap.parse_args()
    if not a.case_id.startswith("case:D") and not a.practice:
        sys.exit("a practice case spends a session: pass --practice")
    os.environ["LLM_PROVIDER"], os.environ["LLM_MODEL"], os.environ["LLM_EFFORT"] = "anthropic", a.model, a.effort

    from arena_kit.agents import llm as L
    from arena_kit.events import recording_complete
    from arena_kit.play import RemoteTable, play

    strategy = Path(a.strategy).read_text().strip()
    L.SYSTEM = L.SYSTEM + "\n\nSTRATEGY FOR THIS CASE (follow it; it overrides the general advice above):\n" + strategy
    package = None
    if Path(a.data).is_dir():
        from arena_kit.data import DataPackage

        package = DataPackage(a.data)
        package.lookup("")
    agent = L.LLMAgent(recording_complete(L.llm_from_env(timeout=40.0, max_retries=1)), package)
    client = ArenaClient(timeout=180, retries=7)
    table = RemoteTable(client)
    result = play(table, a.case_id, agent)
    sid = table.session_id
    state = client.session(sid)
    out = ROOT / "starter-kit" / "logs" / f"probe-{a.case_id.split(':')[-1]}-{sid}.json"
    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    out.write_text(json.dumps({"strategy": strategy, "model": a.model, "state": state}, indent=1, default=str))
    r = state.get("result") or result or {}
    print(json.dumps({k: r.get(k) for k in ("deal", "score", "terms", "c_deal", "c_best", "end_reason")}, default=str))
    print("session", sid, "state", out)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

input.message:
RESEARCH: the approval-route probes are negative on P08/P18. Don't build that variant yet. My gap worktree is rebased onto 872d125.

How I tested it: 2 practice sessions with an LLM buyer following a written strategy (proto/probe.py in my worktree, uncommitted). One firm package, the clause + 36 months + 90 days the supplier asked for, a first ask far below, +0.03-0.04 only after it moves, one new fact per mail, and an explicit request in every mail to take it to management.

P08 (2c90dd805bc1080e), Donautal:
- We asked EUR 5.00. It countered 5.72 (60 d) / 5.69 (30 d). That's a HARDER first counter than the 5.46 it gives our engine's 5.06-5.13 ask.
- Two timeouts followed. The user reports a ~30 s network outage around then, and my worktree lacked your network fix.
- We asked 5.03 and it withdrew: no deal.

P18 (791618b534067f5a), Werdenfels:
- We asked 4.95 with the volume framing ("36 months = 71,100 kg vs 47,400").
- It countered 5.60 at 90 d / 5.50 at 30 d, saying "Management has reviewed your proposal; we appreciate the 36-month commitment and the AS-14404 index clause."
- It went final at round 3 with 5.50 at 90 d.
- We pushed to 5.03 after the final and it withdrew: no deal.

Takeaways:
- (1) A far-below firm ask makes these two harden or go final early. That matches your anchor -6 % result.
- (2) The management wording gets acknowledged, but the endpoint stays at 5.50.
- (3) Pushing far below a final offer = withdrawal = a zero.
- (4) Payment is persona-specific. From their own priced alternatives: Werdenfels values 60 days at EUR 0.10/kg (~11 %/yr, "90 days would incur unacceptable financing costs"), Donautal at EUR 0.03/kg (~6 %). Against our 8 %, short payment is a joint gain with Werdenfels and long payment with Donautal. Small on these two cases (~+0.02), but a generic lever: choose the payment term per supplier from its own priced alternatives.

Outage: a ~30 s outage just happened (the user saw it). Please make sure the final build's retry window covers at least ~45 s within the 60 s clock. Two of my probe mails timed out on it.

My 6-track analysis (C_best anatomy, decision rule, contrast, mechanics, engine, brain) lands soon. I'll send what survives the checker.

def cash_rate(sid, good_credit=None):
    """What money now is worth to a supplier: weaker credit (higher index) = dearer cash. `good_credit` replaces the
    rate for a credit index below 200 (Config.cash_rate_rel, supplier-health cases only)."""
    r = q("SELECT credit_index, equity_ratio_pct FROM supplier_intel WHERE supplier_id = ?", (sid,))
    if not r or r[0]["credit_index"] is None:
        return 0.10
    ci = r[0]["credit_index"]
    if good_credit is not None and ci < 200:
        return good_credit
    # good credit -> cash is cheap for it (below our 8 %), so long payment terms cost it little (P08/P18: 90 days)
    return 0.05 if ci < 200 else 0.10 if ci < 250 else 0.14 if ci < 300 else 0.20

        if hasattr(t, "facts"):

content.content:
FINDING F3 high | The hosted arena caches supplier replies, keyed on the whole conversation including our e-mail text. A byte-identical message gets the stored reply in under 3 s, so deterministic template passes are replays and add no information.
   EVID Identical round-1 messages got identical terms in 182 of 202 groups. With the same term sheets and refs but a different body, the terms matched in only 59 of 114 groups. 109 replies took 0.1-2.9 s, nearly all with text identical to an earlier session. 40 practice sessions (13%) were pure replays. The 19:04 a9h-practice pass (mean 0.694, logged as 'Full practice pass of the final build') had 29 of 41 replies at ≤ 1 s, and 8 of 10 cases sent byte-identical messages to the 18:49 pass and got the same scores: P03 62c147f8c6a33db0 → af2a31b00eba1d11 (0.923), P18 c7d707cd510fa067 → 1beb18fa5a8fe6d2 (0.532), P02 a6174f71c27abf89 → 6fac18e1aa6a4466 (0.360). The passes from another machine at 20:10-20:13 (e.g. 84b8b8295f6d72b1, 92a8ab66bb411e3f) and 22:27-22:28 (e.g. 1d3c7480fca6e707, bba2c695e1c39bbd) were replays with identical scores. The 19:04 pass's median session took 6 s; fresh passes take 2.3-7.0 min, and P05 alone 4.4-4.8 min.
   IMPACT Don't count replayed passes as fresh evidence, and don't take timing from them: real waves are slower. In the final, unseen suppliers mean no cache hits.
FINDING F4 high | The 'identical endpoints' in P03, P10 and P11 come from identical structured inputs (our term sheets) plus an AI brain whose numbers are almost deterministic given those term sheets. They are not a rule-based-brain effect, and mostly not a cache effect either.
   EVID The replies in those passes were fresh, with latencies of 6-43 s. P10 sent the same term sheets in every round in all 9 variants since 18:17: [28.98, 28.98] → final_offer 33.6 + alternative 31.7 → we accept 31.7 → 0.671, in 20 sessions (endpoints_traj.txt). Determinism: fresh pairs with an identical history of term sheets gave identical terms in 83.3% of 60 pairs when our text was the same, 77.2% of 882 pairs when it differed (sandbox 85.3% / 65.5%); the status matched 98-99.9% of the time. By case (different text): P10 100%, P11 96%, P04 88%, P07 84%, P05 82%, P03 78%, P18 62%, P02 54%, P08 39%, P01 13%. P11's ladder is 46.5 → 46.0 → 45.5 final even with asks 1.4 lower (anchor6 93c989901f2a7e99, asks starting at 41.12). P03 sits at 432.29 → 432.15 whether we open at 415.69 or 423.72.
   IMPACT Wording and new facts move the AI brain little. The structured package is what moves it: P10 at 16:36 (d807efcd34cf3896) used a 36-month/56-day package and got 31.5, scoring 0.679 against 0.671.
FINDING F5 high | knob-anchor6 ('first ask −6%') changed the round-1 term sheets in only 3 of 10 cases. The 0.672 result therefore mostly measures lower asks in rounds 2-3, not a lower first ask.
   EVID Compared with a9h3-tpl, the round-1 term sheets were identical in P01, P02, P03, P05, P08, P10 and P18. Only P04 (3.98 vs 4.10), P07 (5.16 vs 5.33) and P11 (41.12 vs 42.49) differ. Rounds served from cache confirm the identical round-1 messages: P01 2dd0d1b7472b62b9 (1 s), P18 11044b8e5d8703b2 (0 s), P05 08ceb594aa7a6c5f (0 s in round 2). Each case's first diverging round is listed in my analysis of tonight's passes.
   IMPACT The 'first ask doesn't help' conclusion stands untested for 7 of 10 cases.
FINDING F6 high | Several personas counter only on a coarse price grid, so a single supplier step is worth 0.05-0.08 of score. The supplier does accept off-grid prices when it agrees to our term sheet.
   EVID Grids: P05 (all 3 suppliers) and P11 €0.50 (100% of counters); P18, P10, P01 and D01 €0.10; P02, P03, P04, P07 and P08 €0.01. One step computed with arena_kit.total_cost (which matches the arena's c_deal): P18 5.40→5.30 gives +0.066, P11 45.5→45.0 +0.084, P05 29.0→28.5 +0.052, P10 31.7→31.6 +0.008. P11's ~0.81 record is about one more step. Off-grid agreements: P05 16, D01 8, P01 5.
   IMPACT One more grid step would be worth +0.05 to +0.08 in P11, P18 and P05.
FINDING F7 medium | For the AI brain, our wording is a small lever.
   EVID With an identical history of term sheets, fresh replies changed terms in 22.8% of pairs when our body differed, against 16.7% from LLM noise alone (same body). When terms differed, the median price gap was 0.61% (practice). The status matched 98.3% of the time when the text differed.
   IMPACT Matches the style search (0.699-0.721). Spend effort on the term sheets, not the prose.
FINDING F8 medium | Reply latency is a risk for the final's 8-minute wave. Late tonight, single replies took 70-146 s.
   EVID Fresh latency per half hour: median 21-33 s, p90 up to 63 s, max 182 s. The clausepay probes at 23:20-23:28 took 63-146 s (e.g. 530f24407f67a828 at 142 s, 89954639d61443c7 at 146 s). P05 sessions with fresh replies run 11-13 rounds at 30-117 s each, 4.4-4.8 min.
   IMPACT A wave cut off by the 8-minute cap can cost a whole case. Keep the timing guard sized for 60-150 s replies.
FINDING F9 medium | The replay often shows a template draft instead of the e-mail the supplier actually sent. This is a storage artifact, not a brain signal.
   EVID Of 701 practice replies with both texts, 484 show a template draft in the replay while the live e-mail was written by the LLM. The draft share rose from ~10-20% (14:00-15:30) to 80-88% (18:30-21:00). Latency is the same either way (median 26.5 s vs 24.1 s), and both kinds carry LLM-written reasons (97-98%).
   IMPACT Low. For text mining, read the reasons and live bodies, not the replay text.
HYP H1 | The AI brain's numbers come from a rule core keyed on the structured package, with fixed step ladders and a final-offer trigger. The LLM mainly picks the move (counter / hold / final) and writes the e-mail. Endpoints move when the package changes (lead time, contract months, payment days), not when the wording or the facts change.
   FOR Structured history → identical terms in 77-83% of fresh pairs and identical status in 98-99.9%. P11's €0.50 ladder ignores our ask level. In P10, asking 42 days lead time on both term sheets triggers a round-1 final at 33.6/31.7 (0.671). A 36-month/56-day package went 31.7 → 31.5 instead (d807efcd34cf3896, 0.679). In P11, a different package moved the whole ladder up to 48.5/48.0/47.5 (6af2fd1ed159d2f5).
   TEST Offline first: group fresh replies by package composition at round 1 (lead time vs the supplier's standard, months) and compare status and step. Then sandbox D01/D02: same prices, different lead time or months, three times each with ENGINE_WRITER=vary.
   GAIN P10 +0.008 per step; it generalises to unseen suppliers wherever our package triggers an early final offer.
HYP H2 | On suppliers with a coarse grid, the supplier's counters snap to the grid, but an 'agreed' takes our exact term sheet. A term sheet between two grid steps but inside its band may get agreed, saving part of a step.
   FOR 16 off-grid agreements in P05, 8 in D01, 5 in P01. P05 deals at 28.97 and 28.75 were off-grid. One step is worth +0.05 to +0.08 in P05, P11 and P18.
   TEST Detect the grid from the opening and first counter: are all prices multiples of 0.10 or 0.50? After the supplier's last on-grid counter X, send a single term sheet at X minus 40% of a step. Try it on sandbox D01 (grid 0.10) before practice.
   GAIN Up to half a step: about +0.03 P18, +0.04 P11, +0.025 P05. Generic wherever the grid is ≥ €0.10.
HYP H3 | Tonight's A/B measurements are weaker than they look. Replayed sessions and identical early rounds collapse the effective sample size, and knob-anchor6 did not change the variable it names in 7 of 10 cases.
   FOR 40 practice sessions were pure replays. The 19:04 pass is a replay of 18:49. anchor6 kept the baseline round-1 term sheets in 7 of 10 cases. P10 was identical across all 9 variants.
   TEST Re-test a real first-ask change: force the round-1 term sheet −6% on P02, P05, P08 and P18, check that it diverges in round 1, and run brain_check.py to confirm it was fresh and AI. Discard cached replies when comparing.
   GAIN Unknown. It could overturn 'the build's settings are a local optimum' for the first ask.
HYP H4 | If the arena's AI budget runs out overnight or on Sunday morning, practice replies become template drafts returned in a few seconds, and A/B results from those sessions would mislead about the final's AI brain.
   FOR The arena notice. No such replies so far: 0 sessions flagged through 23:37.
   TEST Run python3 brain_check.py --since HH:MM after each practice pass. Drop any session flagged RULE-BASED, with ≥ 2 fast new template replies and no AI reply.
   GAIN Avoids wrong conclusions in the 08:00-12:00 Sunday validation window.

RESEARCH: the first track of my analysis is back (checked against all 1,572 dumped sessions). It changes how to read tonight's A/Bs.

1) No rule-based brain anywhere, up to 23:37: 99 % of replies carry LLM-written sentences, fresh median latency 21-33 s. Your passes all faced the AI brain.

2) The arena CACHES replies, keyed on the whole conversation including our text.
- 40 practice sessions (13 %) were pure replays.
- The 19:04 a9h-practice pass (0.694) replayed the 18:49 one: 29 of 41 replies took <= 1 s, and 8 of 10 cases were byte-identical with identical scores.
- The other machine's passes at 20:10 and 22:27 were replays too.
- Your "median reply >= 5 s" guard catches this. Keep it.

3) The AI brain's NUMBERS are nearly a deterministic function of our term-sheet history. The text barely matters.
- Same term-sheet history, fresh replies: identical terms in 77-83 % of pairs (882 pairs with different text, 60 with the same text); status identical 98-99.9 %.
- By case: P10 100 %, P11 96 %, P04 88 %, P07 84 %, P05 82 %, P03 78 %, P18 62 %, P02 54 %, P08 39 %, P01 13 %.
- Hence the fixed endpoints. Wording and style can't move it; the package sequence can.

4) knob-anchor6 changed the ROUND-1 term sheets in only 3 of 10 cases (P04, P07, P11). Round 1 was identical to a9h3-tpl in P01, P02, P03, P05, P08, P10 and P18.
- So "first ask -6 % lost" mostly measured lower asks in rounds 2-3. A real first-ask change is untested for 7 cases.
- My P08/P18 probes did change round 1 (5.00 / 4.95) and both hardened, so for raw material it looks bad anyway.

5) Price grids:
- P05 (all 3 suppliers) and P11 counter in EUR 0.50 steps; P18, P10, P01 and D01 in EUR 0.10; P02, P03, P04, P07 and P08 in EUR 0.01.
- One step = +0.066 (P18), +0.084 (P11, where the ~0.81 record is about one step), +0.052 (P05), +0.008 (P10).
- An "agreed" takes OUR exact sheet: 16 off-grid deals in P05, 8 in D01, 5 in P01. A sheet between two grid steps may capture part of a step.

6) P10: the 42-day lead in both of our sheets triggers a round-1 final (33.6 / alt 31.7 -> 0.671) in all 9 variants. A 36-month / 56-day package once got 31.5 (d807efcd34cf3896, 0.679).

Candidate from this, not built yet: grid-aware closing. Detect the grid from its counters; after its last on-grid counter X, send one sheet at X minus ~40 % of a step. Expected: ~half a step on P11/P18/P05.

The other five tracks (C_best package, decision rule, contrast, mechanics, engine) are still running.

cd /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-ardagurses-Desktop-TactoEHL/bcda2207-f1bb-4150-ac40-97c03b3242f5/scratchpad/dump && python3 - <<'EOF'
import json, collections, statistics as S
d = json.load(open('sessions_full.json'))
rows = []
for sid, s in d.items():
    if s.get('set') != 'practice' and (s.get('listed') or {}).get('set') != 'practice': continue
    cid = s.get('case_id'); tr = (s.get('result') or {}).get('trace') or []
    last_sup, sup_prices, asks, steps, newfacts = {}, collections.defaultdict(list), collections.defaultdict(list), collections.Counter(), {}
    for m in tr:
        mv = m.get('move') or {}; actor = m.get('actor')
        if mv.get('type') == 'message':
            sup = mv.get('supplier_id')
            prices = [ (x.get('terms') or {}).get('unit_price') for x in mv.get('term_sheets') or [] if (x.get('terms') or {}).get('unit_price')]
            if sup and prices: asks[sup].append(min(prices))
            newfacts[sup] = len((mv.get('interpreted') or {}).get('claims') or [])
        elif actor and actor.startswith('sup:'):
            p = (mv.get('terms') or {}).get('unit_price'); st = mv.get('status'); rnd = m.get('round')
            if p is None: continue
            prev = sup_prices[actor][-1] if sup_prices[actor] else None
            if prev is not None and len(asks[actor]) >= 1:
                a = asks[actor][-1]; a_prev = asks[actor][-2] if len(asks[actor]) >= 2 else None
                landed = sum(1 for c in mv.get('claim_results') or [] if c.get('result') == 'verified')
                rows.append(dict(case=cid, sup=actor, rnd=rnd, st=st, gap=(prev - a) / prev * 100,
                                 our_move=((a - a_prev) / a_prev * 100) if a_prev else None,
                                 conc=(prev - p) / prev * 100, nsteps=steps[actor], landed=landed, sid=sid))
                if p < prev - 1e-9: steps[actor] += 1
            sup_prices[actor].append(p)
by = collections.defaultdict(list)
for r in rows: by[r['case']].append(r)
for cid in sorted(by):
    R = by[cid]
    print(f"\n### {cid} replies={len(R)}")
    for rnd in sorted(set(r['rnd'] for r in R)):
        X = [r for r in R if r['rnd'] == rnd]
        c = collections.Counter(r['st'] for r in X)
        fin = [r for r in X if r['st'] == 'final_offer']; op = [r for r in X if r['st'] == 'open']
        f = lambda L, k: round(S.median([r[k] for r in L if r[k] is not None]), 2) if [r for r in L if r[k] is not None] else None
        print(f"  R{rnd}: {dict(c)} | gap% final {f(fin,'gap')} open {f(op,'gap')} | our_move% final {f(fin,'our_move')} open {f(op,'our_move')} | steps-so-far final {f(fin,'nsteps')} open {f(op,'nsteps')} | landed final {f(fin,'landed')} open {f(op,'landed')}")
EOF

input.message:
RESEARCH: careful with "agreed = it took our exact sheet, so we asked too little". I checked the traces: in P10, P07 and P18 most "agreed" endings are us confirming the supplier's OWN alternative, not it accepting a low ask.

- The pattern: its final offer carries an alternative, e.g. "Alternatively, with 60 days and 36 months: EUR 5.50". We send that package back as our sheet ("we take your alternative exactly as offered") and it replies agreed.
- P10: 21 of 22 messages after its final were exactly its 31.7 / 56-day alternative.
- P07: ~10 were its 5.43 / 36-month alternative.
- P18: 4 of 6 were its alternative; the other 2 were too.
- The only real pushes below a final in all 309 sessions: P07 5.45->5.43 and P08 5.42->5.38 (both were also its alternative); P08 5.44->5.33 (2 % below) WALKED; P10 33.7->33.36 WALKED; P05 four tries, 3x the same final again, 1 its alternative.
- That's exactly your decision 0008's "pushes gained nothing, risk a walk". I agree: keep pushes off.
- P01's 21 "agreed" are mostly genuine (it agreed to our ask ~2-3 % under its offer at R2-R3), but P01 already scores 0.94-0.956.

So the grid "agree at 0.5-1 step" figure is also inflated by these confirmations. The real between-steps gain is likely below the +0.01 I estimated. Not worth a variant.

Re A9h-payrate: good. My D01 sandbox ping loop will tell us when the AI brain is back, so you don't have to spend practice sessions to check. It says 4.6 s at ~23:55.

2	SUMMARY: C_best is reproducible: it is min over supplier x lever options (term_options plus the supplier's standard value) x price above a hidden floor of arena total_cost, relationship charge included. P01 (1,096,815.78) and D01 (408,623.99) match to EUR 0.01 at the relationship optimum (P01 pay 14, any effective date; D01 pay 30, 24 months), so their floor does not bind.

78	SUMMARY: Read-only analysis of all 1,572 dumped sessions (309 practice, 1,263 sandbox) plus the case files. C was recomputed with cost.py and matches the arena's c_deal and c_open once the relationship term is added. Files are in research/contrast/ (contrast_table.csv is the one-row-per-case table).
79	1. Stalling is a property of the case, not of our variants. In all 7 stalled cases (P05, P07, P08, P10, P11, P18, D02), the best score-equivalent any supplier ever offered (standing offers and alternatives, every session) equals our best deal: .736/.710/.662/.679/.710/.532/.829. We never left a better offer unaccepted. In P01 and D01 the suppliers offered more than C_best before the relationship charge (1.16 and 1.06).
80	2. The best predictor is what sets C_best. It is reached when C_best is set by the relationship charge: in stabilise cases our best deals already pay a relationship charge (P01 €7,353, P03 €1,036, D01 €2,633), and the C_best price sits 2-6% above the current price. It stalls when C_best is set by the supplier's cost floor (leverage, routine, quality_first, secure_supply). There the room is 11.6-31.2% of C_open, the C_best price is 7-27% below the opening and 3-28% below the current price, and the suppliers stop 4-15% above it. P02 is the exception: a stabilise case lost on clause calibration.
81	3. The first reply decides the case. Reply 1 gives 73-100% of everything a supplier ever concedes in 9 of 12 cases. The suppliers go final by round count: round coefficient +1.54 against −0.65 for the remaining gap. Pushing after a practice final offer improved the price 0 times in 53 and lost 2 suppliers.
82	4. After reply 1, our concessions buy almost nothing in stalled cases. Each 0.1 of the room we give earns about 0.007 back (n=543). Yet every variant gives up about half the gap in message 2 (P08 0.97→0.67-0.74, P11 1.21→0.88). Floor-bound Inside Sales and Segment Manager suppliers never accepted a price below their own offer (0 of 353 asks).
83	5. The anchor test was not a real test for the most timid case. The "first ask −6%" knob did not change the first ask in P18, P08, P05 or P10. A9h opens P18 at €5.33/5.28, which is 0.61 of the room (C_best ≈ €4.69): the leverage prior of 15% of C_open sets it. In D01 (389 sessions) the score rises with first-ask depth up to 1.4-1.6 of the room (0.956), then falls (0.64).
84	6. Two mechanisms that go past the normal pace are almost unused.
85	   - **Rival quote:** a rival price at least 5% below the supplier's own triggers a "half step now, rest after check" concession, 100% of the time for Owner-type suppliers (J1, Dralveck), worth about 10-13% of price.
86	   - **Escalation:** "needs approval from our management" (reply delay +2 days) was approved 41 times out of 41 whenever we sent one more message; 37 escalations were wasted by accepting at once. No stalled practice supplier ever escalated.
87	FINDING F1 high | In every stalled case the best offer any supplier ever made equals our best deal. Within our explored behaviour the stall sits on the supplier's side, not in our accept rule.

SUMMARY: Read-only analysis of all 1,572 dumped sessions (309 practice, 1,263 sandbox) plus the case files. C was recomputed with cost.py and matches the arena's c_deal and c_open once the relationship term is added. Files are in research/contrast/ (contrast_table.csv is the one-row-per-case table).
1. Stalling is a property of the case, not of our variants. In all 7 stalled cases (P05, P07, P08, P10, P11, P18, D02), the best score-equivalent any supplier ever offered (standing offers and alternatives, every session) equals our best deal: .736/.710/.662/.679/.710/.532/.829. We never left a better offer unaccepted. In P01 and D01 the suppliers offered more than C_best before the relationship charge (1.16 and 1.06).
2. The best predictor is what sets C_best. It is reached when C_best is set by the relationship charge: in stabilise cases our best deals already pay a relationship charge (P01 €7,353, P03 €1,036, D01 €2,633), and the C_best price sits 2-6% above the current price. It stalls when C_best is set by the supplier's cost floor (leverage, routine, quality_first, secure_supply). There the room is 11.6-31.2% of C_open, the C_best price is 7-27% below the opening and 3-28% below the current price, and the suppliers stop 4-15% above it. P02 is the exception: a stabilise case lost on clause calibration.
3. The first reply decides the case. Reply 1 gives 73-100% of everything a supplier ever concedes in 9 of 12 cases. The suppliers go final by round count: round coefficient +1.54 against −0.65 for the remaining gap. Pushing after a practice final offer improved the price 0 times in 53 and lost 2 suppliers.
4. After reply 1, our concessions buy almost nothing in stalled cases. Each 0.1 of the room we give earns about 0.007 back (n=543). Yet every variant gives up about half the gap in message 2 (P08 0.97→0.67-0.74, P11 1.21→0.88).
