SUMMARY: Track "decision": reconstructed the supplier bot's decision procedure from 309 practice + 1,263 sandbox sessions (1,247 / 7,864 supplier replies, 51 back-office templates, 51,878 reason sentences). All practice sessions after 14:00 ran the LLM brain (0 all-template sessions), so the data matches what the final will face. About 300 sandbox sessions were all-template.
1) The first counter decides the case. Measured as a share of the room between the opening and the floor implied by C_best, R1 alone delivers 64% of the room at P08 (final endpoint 69%), 46% at P18 (53%), 45-61% at the P05 owners (66-73%), 73% at P03 and 91% at P04. Later rounds add only 0-7 points, except P11 and P07 (gradual) and P02.
2) The first counter ignores our ask. It moves with what lands in R1. P18 endpoint median 0.509 when a falling cost-driver index landed in R1 (n=23), against 0.311 without (n=8).
3) After R1 the rep is reciprocal (rounds 2+, practice): no move and no new fact means hold 69% of the time and 0% concession. Move plus a landed fact gives a counter 85% of the time and 1.97% mean concession. A move without a fact gives 0.33%. A fact without a move gives 0.25% (but 0.70% at P01, 2.1% at C1, 1.29% at J1).
4) Each persona goes final at a fixed round: P10 R1 (24/30), P18 R3 (30/31), P04 R3 (23/27), P07 R4 (23/29), P11 R4 (17/30), P08 R3-5. The endpoint is a plateau: best-on-table score q50/max is P11 0.71/0.71, P07 0.697/0.71, P18 0.467/0.532, P08 0.586/0.662, P10 0.671/0.679.
5) Escalation exists. It happened 80 times (C1 78, P02 2), at most once per session. Every time the thread continued, the next reply carried an approval (41/41) and a further step: +0.043 score median, vs +0.021 in other late rounds. 39 escalations were thrown away because we accepted at once, including P02 6c1f4006871e6587, scored 0.157. The P02 Pricing Committee approved 350 with a copper clause in R1 (a7d150b5279c1ce3), the deepest P02 price in our sessions.
6) The RFQ rival step fires at most once per supplier, in R1 for owner-run suppliers. It needs a rival price about 5% (J1, 70210) to 15% (70250) below the standing offer. It speeds up the descent but leaves the P05 endpoint unchanged (median 29.5 either way).
7) Fitted supplier economics, exact for the relationship cases: P01 full cost 130.04 at cash rate 0.096; P02 367.60 at 0.066 with floor margin -1.6% (C_best package 365.79, 90 days, no clause), while the rep's own limit sits near +0.5% (where it escalated); P03 395.36 at 0.060, floor 6.8% against an endpoint of 7.57%. Some suppliers price on fixed grids: P18 and P10 in 0.10 steps, P11 and Hrvelec (70240) in 0.50 steps.
8) Untested in 309 sessions: citing news (0 times), sending our own final offer (0), asking for management approval (10 mentions, no explicit request).
FINDING F1 high | Reconstructed state machine of the supplier bot, step by step. (a) It checks each cited fact: verified, irrelevant, contradicted (costs trust) or duplicate. (b) Its persona reacts to a verified fact: either it lands ("took it into account", "We did not know that - a fair point") or it is blocked ("does not change our calculation/position", "That is not our reality", "Your figures confirm our case"). (c) It picks the buyer package it values most and adds any term it insists on, such as an index clause for contracts over 12 months. (d) The rep makes a call: counter, hold, final_offer, accept, walk_away or answer. (e) The rules price the counter; if the counter is at or below the buyer's price it agrees on the buyer's exact terms. (f) If the counter reaches the rep's limit, the status becomes final_offer. (g) Approval-ladder personas escalate once ("The buyer wants more than my band allows. Approve a further step?") and the approval arrives on the next reply. (h) A much lower rival quote triggers "I give half the step now and check the rest"; the rest follows next round, once per session. (i) The price is rounded to the persona's grid. HYP H1 | Close escalation-aware. When a reply says "needs approval from our management" (or committee/approve), never accept on that turn, even if the status is final_offer. Send one more message: same packages plus a minimal move (≥ one grid step if the supplier is quantized) or one new fact. The approved further step arrives on the next reply. Each supplier escalates once per session.
   FOR 41/41 approvals when the thread continued, 0 walk-aways after a message; approval round +0.043 score median vs +0.021; 39 approvals forfeited by closing at once; P02 6c1f4006871e6587 accepted at the band end (0.157); P02 committee approved a huge step in a7d150b5279c1ce3.
   AGAINST The approved step is modest (C1); escalation shows up in only about 6-9% of sessions of ladder suppliers and was never seen at P03, P08 or P11.
   TEST Free on sandbox D02, where C1 escalates in about 9% of sessions. Implement the rule and run until about 10 escalations occur; check approval rate and price drop. Then one practice P02 session with asks at 90 days, no clause, just under 368.
   GAIN +0.04 on approval-ladder suppliers; about +0.003-0.005 on the mean; almost no downside | GEN High: keyed on reply text, not case IDs. 'A group with an approval ladder' is one of the brief's four persona types.
HYP H2 | Maximise the R1 recomputation. Put every fact likely to land into the first message: falling indices for drivers the supplier itself lists in its opening ('X rose … and is N % of our cost'), largest share × fall first, windows of 12 months or less inside the last 12 months; a rival in RFQs; and the levers the supplier signals. Avoid facts that get blocked (rising drivers, own past prices). Keep later rounds for one new landed fact plus a move.
   FOR R1 delivers 64-100% of total concession at P08, P18, P05, P03, P04. P18 endpoint 0.509 vs 0.311 with vs without an R1 falling index landing. P08 never landed an R1 fact: the AS-14404 fall was blocked, and the PPI-C2431 fall (38% share), which does land ('reduces our cost basis… passed on'), was sent only in R2.
   AGAINST The team's fact planner (more facts in later rounds) scored 0.715 = baseline, but that moved facts later, not earlier. Session-level differences are confounded with engine versions. The persona can block a fact (P08's hedge).
   TEST Offline: audit A9h's R1 refs on all 19 case files for falling own-driver indices. Practice: one P08 session with PPI-C2431@2026-05→2026-08 plus every other landing fact in R1 (5.45 is the baseline R1 counter at 90 days/24 months), and one P18 session.
   GAIN +0.03-0.2 on raw-material and leverage cases where an own-driver fall exists | GEN High: drivers and shares come from the supplier's own opening text and facts.json.
HYP H3 | Size the move to the persona. Fact-driven personas (they say 'did not know that - a fair point'; e.g. P01, C1, J1) concede on a new landed fact without our move, so hold the ask and feed one fact per round. Reciprocity personas need our move: never move less than about 0.5% of price or one price-grid step, since smaller moves get holds that burn patience.
   FOR Fact-only concessions: P01 0.70% (100% of rounds), C1 2.1% (98%), J1 1.29%. Moves under 0.5% get small concessions: P07 0.15%, P02 0.11%, P11 0. P11 lost a 0.5 step (46.0 endpoint, 0.626 vs 0.71) after a +0.18 move.
   AGAINST Pooled practice: fact without move averages only 0.25%. Personas must be detected from R1-R2 text, which is noisy.
   TEST Sandbox D01 (F1 reacts to facts) and D02: variant 'hold ask + new fact' vs 'move + fact'. Compare buyer concession per supplier concession and the endpoint.
   GAIN +0.02-0.08 on fact-driven and quantized suppliers | GEN High: keyed on reaction templates the arena prints verbatim.
HYP H4 | Ask explicitly for escalation. When the rep reaches its limit (counter unchanged or 'limit of what our cost structure allows'), ask it to take one concrete package near our target to its management or pricing committee, with a business reason (full-volume multi-year award). Aim at group-owned suppliers (supplier_intel owner_type=group).
   FOR The engine has a working escalation path to boss roles (Owner, Pricing Committee); a P02 committee approval produced the deepest P02 deal; NoIdea's P02 record (0.847) needs about 366.5 at 90 days, which is below the rep's band end (about 368.5) and above the floor (365.8), so only an approved step reaches it. P08 Donautal is group-owned.
   AGAINST Escalation looks rule-triggered (computed counter below the band end), not text-triggered. 10 practice messages with approval wording had no effect. P03 (group) has its price reductions frozen by management.
   TEST Two practice sessions (P02 at 90 days with no clause, P08) using the explicit request at the rep's limit. Watch for back-office 'Approve a further step?'. Check the session ran on the LLM brain (free-text reasons present).
   GAIN Unknown; if it works, +0.1-0.16 on P02-type cases | GEN Medium: only suppliers with a boss role.
HYP H5 | In RFQs, trigger the rival step in R1 for every bidder: cite the lowest verifiable rival price (any rival's round-0 offer ID; only price is checked, so it may miss our must-haves) to every other supplier in the first message. Accept immediately when a 'checked' reply agrees below its standing offer.
   FOR Owner-run suppliers fire the step only in R1 and only once. It did not fire when we cited 34.0-36.0 to 70250, but did at 32.5. The cheapest P05 opening, Hrvelec 31.5 (52-day lead), was not used as the R1 lever under A9h's compliant-lead rule.
   AGAINST The endpoint was unchanged (70250 median 29.5 either way; J1 about -0.3); records (TTMAR P05 0.924, about 27.3) need more than this step.
   TEST Free on sandbox D02: cite the cheapest rival opening in R1 to all bidders and measure the R1-2 trigger rate (J1 already about 65%).
   GAIN +0.0-0.03 on RFQs; protects against missed triggers | GEN High for RFQs.
HYP H6 | Track alternatives. Every offer:…-a alternative is a standing, acceptable package until replaced. Accept the best by C when it beats the expected next step. Never revert asks to earlier figures.
   FOR P01 f2801e4bbae1fcc7 lost a 0.98 alternative and closed at 0.947; reverting asks drew an immediate final.
   AGAINST Rare (1-2 sessions); A9h may already recall the best offer.
   TEST Offline replay of all practice traces through the engine's accept logic: count sessions where a better standing alternative existed at close.
   GAIN +0.0-0.03 occasionally | GEN High.
HYP H7 | Do not fight a near-monopolist. Allocation, full order book or 'far below any calculation' means it goes final in R1-R2 and barely moves (10-12% of the room). Make one strong R1 move with its standard lead and volume, then accept the best standing offer early instead of risking a walk.
   FOR P10: final at R1 in 24/30 sessions, endpoint 0.671 in nearly every session, a push after its final led to withdrawal (5491b900c6865fc0). 70240 moved 10% of the room and walked at R5 (783e0a6bcbfe0ce9).
   AGAINST No upside evidence; this protects against zeros only.
   TEST Offline: classify from news topic (allocation, full_order_book) plus R1 status final_offer; confirm on the 9 unseen case files.
   GAIN Avoids about 0.67-point zeros on such cases | GEN High: news topics are in facts.json, plus Sunday's release.
HYP H8 | Validate tonight's practice tests against the rule-based fallback brain. If the arena's AI budget runs out, practice replies come from the rule brain and the results will not transfer to the final.
   FOR Arena notice tonight. In our dump, about 300 of 1,263 sandbox sessions are all-template, while 0 practice sessions after 14:00 are.
   AGAINST None.
   TEST For every new practice session, require at least one reason sentence outside the known template list (reasons_vocab.txt); otherwise discard the result.
   GAIN Prevents wrong conclusions | GEN High.
HYP H9 | Send our own credible final offer at the target, with a deadline, once the rep is at its limit. The LLM rep may accept a package above its floor rather than lose the deal.
   FOR Never tried (0 of 1,158 messages). C_best for leverage cases sits 26-58% of the room below the plateaus, so the floor is not binding at the endpoint.
   AGAINST Agreement seems to require our ask to be at or above the rep's computed counter. Pushes after a final were withdrawn 2 of 5 times. There is walk risk on unseen suppliers.
   TEST One practice session each on P08 and P11 after the supplier's final: send its final package minus one grid step as 'our final offer, valid today'.
   GAIN Unknown, high variance | GEN Medium, risky.
====================================================================================================
SUMMARY: I mapped every buyer lever and bot mechanic against 309 practice and 1,263 sandbox sessions from the dump, plus /v1/live (public; it gives the per-case records and the € saved). The local cost function reproduces the arena's c_deal to the cent in all 1,123 deals checked.
1. RFQ rival unlock. The first verified "much lower" rival offer makes a supplier give half a step (P05 13.8 % of C, D02 11.2 %). It gives the rest in its next reply (5.8 % / 6.5 %), even if that next move is a timeout. It fires at most once per supplier. It never fired for Hrvelec (0 of 29 rival citations).
2. Lead time is the biggest positive-sum lever we leave unused. Suppliers that open with a long lead charge 0.47-0.56 % of price per day of acceleration (P10 23 of 23 alternatives, P05 Hrvelec 10, D02 C1 33). Our late cost is a flat €/day (P05 €200, P10 €2,400). The A9h lead_cap only allows leads up to our need, so Hrvelec got 35-day sheets 144 times and 42-day sheets only 14 times. Its price at 35 days was 32.5-34.0, against 31.5-32.0 at 42 days. 42 days would have cost us only €1,400 (0.017 score).
3. Final-offer mechanics. After a final offer, a timeout ends the thread 77 of 81 times; a message with no term sheet keeps it alive 29 of 29 times; a lower price ask got 13 walk-aways in 77 tries for ≤0.5 % gain. Sending back the supplier's own alternative is always agreed (156 of 156). A9h has rfq_hold switched off.
4. Escalation. Bigger moves go to the boss: "Approve a further step?" was approved in 41 of 41 D02 cases that had a next round, worth +1.29 % of C. In practice it fired only twice (P02). Once we accepted the final offer before the approval could arrive. Our 11 practice e-mails that mention approval all told the rep to stay within its own authority.
5. Contract length is worth 0 to the bots: 24 vs 36 months changed the price by 0.00 % in 8 of 8 alternatives. Payment alternatives give each supplier's cash rate directly (P01 13.7 %, P02 6.6 %, P18 0 %).
6. Final offers come when no fact lands: 34-42 % final without a landing fact, 0-8 % with one. Suppliers never walk while open (33 of 36 practice walk-aways followed timeouts).
7. Never used in 1,158 practice e-mails: 'our final offer', walk-away or BATNA lines, budget, a dated deadline. Cost-breakdown requests: 393 asks, 0 files from practice suppliers.
8. Records back-solved from € saved: P05 0.965 = €26.67 (14 d pay, 28 d lead); P18 0.727 = €5.10-5.15; P11 0.885 = about €44.5; P10 0.702 = €31.91 at 42 d. Our P05 endpoint is €28.75-29.50 in every pass.
FINDING F1 high | RFQ rival unlock: when a buyer cites a verified 'much lower' rival offer, the supplier gives half a step now and the rest in its next reply, at most once per supplier.
   EVID Back office 'The buyer shows a much lower rival quote. I give half the step now and check the rest' and next round 'Checked: give the rest of the step'. It fires at most once per supplier per session: P05 70210 25x, 70250 5x, 70240 0x; D02 J1 558x, C1 154x. Half step: P05 13.8% of C (n=30), D02 11.2% (n=596). Rest in the next reply: P05 5.8%, D02 6.5%. The rest also came after timeouts (P05 29/30 rests, D02 598/598). The reply carries the cue 'We need to clarify this internally - we will come back to you on price' (practice: next round +5.83% C, n=29). Example: b371991467d124b0, where 70210 went 36.0 -> 30.5 -> agreed 29.27. Triggering is persona-dependent: 70210 fired on 23/27 first citations at a 4-6% gap; 70250 on 5/28 at 10%+; Hrvelec (capacity-full exporter) on 0/29 citations of any gap.
   IMPACT Worth 15-20% of C per unlocked bidder; RFQ only. Already used in P05; the open risk is a bidder that is never unlocked or a case closed before the rest reply.
FINDING F2 high | Suppliers that open with a lead time longer than our need charge about 0.5% of price per day of acceleration. Our late cost is a flat € per day, so A9h's lead_cap (only up to need) and its target model (supplier extra=0) leave a positive-sum lever unused.
   EVID Alternatives that differ only in lead time: P10 70410 +12 days -> -5.65% price (23/23, -0.47%/day); P05 70240 +17 days -> -8.8% (6x), +10 days -> -4.6 to -6.2% (-0.54%/day); D02 C1 -0.56%/day (n=33); D02 J1 (opens at 28 d) 0%. Openings: Hrvelec 52 d, Ravensteiner 54 d, C1 standard 45 d. late_cost_per_day: P05 €200, D02 €150, P10 €2,400, P09 €1,800. P05: 42 vs 35 days costs €1,400 (0.017 score); we sent Hrvelec 35-day sheets 144x (priced 32.5-34.0) and 42-day sheets 14x (31.5-32.0). D02 C1 deals at 42 d scored 0.383 (n=16) vs 0.276 at 35 d (n=32). P10 deals already sit at 54/56 d (25/27) because Ravensteiner offers that alternative itself.
   IMPACT About 3% of price on a long-lead bidder in RFQ/capacity cases; can decide which bidder wins (+0.02-0.10 per affected case).
FINDING F3 high | After a final_offer: a timeout kills the thread, a message without a term sheet keeps it alive, a lower price ask risks a walk-away, and the supplier's own alternative is always agreed.
   EVID Timeout after final_offer: walked 20/20 in practice, 57/61 in sandbox. Message without a term sheet after final: final_offer kept 29/29 (gain 0). Same terms, lower price after final: practice 2/5 walked (5491b900c6865fc0, P10) and 0 gain; sandbox 11/72 walked, +0.2-0.5%. Our single term sheet equal to the supplier's alternative: agreed 156/156 (practice 47, sandbox 109); after a final offer 45/45 with +1.93% C. In practice 33/36 supplier walk-aways followed timeouts, 2 followed pushes after a final offer, and only 1 came while the supplier was open (783e0a6bcbfe0ce9, P05 70240 round 5).
   IMPACT Robustness in RFQ waves: A9h has rfq_hold=False, so a resting final-offer thread is lost after 60 s.
FINDING F4 medium | Boss-approval escalation exists and pays one round later, but our agents never invite it; in practice it fired only twice.
   EVID 'The buyer wants more than my band allows. Approve a further step?': D02 C1 78x, approved in 41/41 cases that had a next round ('Approved: you may go further, within our rules'), next-round concession +1.29% C. Practice: only P02 Nordmark (group). a7d150b5279c1ce3 round 1 -> agreed €350 clause package. 6c1f4006871e6587 round 5 -> final_offer with 'Any further step needs approval from our management' -> we accepted, so the approval round was never collected. 11 practice e-mails told reps the package fits 'within your own approval/authority'; 0 asked them to escalate. Escalation probability rises with the supplier's cumulative concession (D02: 1.4% of messages after <2% conceded vs 8-12% after 4-8% conceded).
   IMPACT Unknown size; likely +1% of C on group/approval-ladder suppliers when collected.
FINDING F5 high | Bots price contract length at zero; payment-only alternatives reveal each supplier's cash rate; the clause deadband is a wash.
   EVID 24<->36 months: 0.00% price change in 8/8 alternatives (P07, P08, P10, P18). Payment alternatives give implied cash rates per year: P01 13.7% (90->30 d -2.29%, n=14), P07 7.5-8.6%, P04 7.3%, P02 6.6% (n=61, matches the team's health-charge estimate), P08 6.5%, P03 4.1%, P18 0% (n=8), P05 30->14 d -1.67% (n=1, ~38%). Our cost of money is 8%. Deadband 0->5%: +2.21% price (P08, n=19) and +1.98% (P18, n=11), about equal to our saving of ~2.25% of spend.
   IMPACT Small (+0.01-0.03): pay fast only for suppliers whose implied rate is above 8% (P01-type), take 90 days otherwise, never pay price for extra contract months.
FINDING F6 high | Final offers are triggered by e-mails without a landing fact. Distinct windows of one index series count as new facts; only identical ID pairs are duplicates, also across RFQ bidders.
   EVID Practice, rounds 2+ (P05 excluded): moved/no new fact 42% final (n=198); held/no new fact 34% (n=29); moved/verified but not landed 17%; held/verified but not landed 5%; moved/landed 8% (n=108); held/landed 0% final and 41% agreed (n=44; P01 17/24). Index claims: 167 new-window and 131 supplier's-own-series claims verified; 126 duplicates, all for an ID pair already cited in the session (102 of them to another supplier). Forecasts: only one volume_change per part per case (other fc snapshots of the same part came back duplicate in P08/P18).
   IMPACT Each landing fact buys about one more open round; the team's planner showed this changes the path more than the endpoint.
FINDING F7 high | Several levers and signals are dead or never tried: cost-breakdown requests, citing a dearer alternative quote, and text signals (final offer, BATNA, deadline, budget).
   EVID 393 practice e-mails asked for a cost breakdown and got 0 XLSX (only the D02 demo bots sent one, 1,167x). What they do reveal is 'Material accounts for about X % of our cost'. Our dearer alternative quote cited to the supplier: verified but 'does not change our calculation' / 'priced higher than our initial offer' (P11, P18). 'A binding higher volume would help us and can improve the price' appears in every practice case (P05 45x, P11 45x, P02 40x), but volume is fixed in 8/10 hosted cases. P05 should-cost cost:320070 = €36.87 is above every quote (31.5-38.5), so citing it only supports the supplier. Never used in 1,158 practice e-mails: 'our final offer' 0, walk-away/BATNA 0, budget 0, dated deadline 4.
   IMPACT Removing dead text has no score effect; the untested text levers are the only unexplored input to the persona LLM.
FINDING F8 medium | The record deals sit 2-8% below our fixed endpoints on price, and in P05 the suppliers agreed to every ask we made right after the half step, so their floor was never probed.
   EVID From /v1/live saved_eur (score check exact): P05 0.965 -> C 226,289 = €26.67 at 14 d/28 d (ours €28.75-29.50 in all 32 deals, every one at 28 d lead and 30/32 at 14 d pay); P18 0.727 -> €5.10-5.15 no clause (ours 5.40); P11 0.885 -> ~€44.5-44.6 (ours 45.50); P10 0.702 -> €31.91 at 42 d / €31.20 at 56 d (ours 31.50 at 56 d); P03 0.963 -> €430.76 at 90 d. P05 round after the half step: asks 28.97-29.97 agreed 11x; asks 27.81-29.22 countered at a fixed 29.50 17x. D02 round after the half step: asks 12%+ below the standing price drew 7.9% moves vs 4.9% for 8-12% (r=0.49, n=561).
   IMPACT P05 gap 0.23 to the record; P18 0.2; P11 0.17.
FINDING F9 high | The reply signals are deterministic status labels, not hidden information.
   EVID validity_days 7 <=> final_offer (174/174 practice, 622 sandbox); 14 <=> agreed/walked; reply_delay_days is a constant per supplier (P05/P11 4 d, P02/P03/P04/P07/P08 1 d, P01/P10/P18 2 d), +1 at a final offer.
   IMPACT None directly; only useful for parsing the status.
FINDING F10 low | Caveat: some of tonight's practice replies may come from the rule-based fallback brain or the reply cache, so endpoints measured then may not carry over to the final.
   EVID Share of practice replies with at least one LLM-written (unique) reason: 84-96% in most hours, but 33% at 18:00-19:00 and 67% at 22:00. WHAT THE BOT IS (four independent tracks agree):
1) R1 is a RECOMPUTATION that sets 64-100 % of the outcome. It mostly ignores our ask and moves with what LANDS in R1.
- P08's R1 counter is 5.45-5.52 whether we ask 5.06 or 5.43.
- P18's endpoint median is 0.509 when a falling own-driver index landed in R1 (n=23), vs 0.311 without (n=8).
- P08 NEVER landed a fact in R1. AS-14404 is blocked ("covered at fixed prices"); the PPI-C2431 fall (38 % share) does land ("reduces our cost basis... passed on"), but A9h sends it only in R2.
2) After R1 each persona goes final at a fixed round (P10 R1, P18 R3 30/31, P04 R3, P07/P11 R4, P08 R3-5). Rounds 2+ are reciprocal:
- move + landed fact: counter 85 %, 1.97 % mean concession;
- move only: 0.33 %;
- neither: hold 69 %.
- Moves smaller than one grid step / ~0.5 % get holds (P11 lost a whole 0.50 step after a +0.18 move: 0.626).
3) ESCALATION is real and we waste it:
- "The buyer wants more than my band allows. Approve a further step?" Whenever the thread continued with one more message, the next reply carried the approval: 41/41, median +0.043 score, 0 walk-aways.
- 39 approvals were thrown away by accepting at once, incl. P02 6c1f4006871e6587 (accepted at the band end, 0.157).
- The P02 committee approved 350 + clause in a7d150b5279c1ce3, the deepest P02 price.
- Approval-ladder personas are one of the brief's persona types, so unseen suppliers will have it.
4) RFQ rival unlock:
- A verified rival >= ~5 % below the recipient's standing offer gives a half step now, "We need to clarify this internally - we will come back to you on price", then the rest next reply (even after a timeout). Once per supplier.
- Owner types fire in R1 (J1 100 % at 5-20 %, Dralveck 100 % at 5-10 %); Hrvelec never fires.
- P05 rest round: our asks 28.97-29.97 were all agreed at once, so the floor was never probed. Record 26.67-27.0 vs our 28.75-29.5.
5) Lead time: long-lead suppliers charge ~0.5 %/day for acceleration (66 alternatives: P10, Hrvelec, C1); our late cost is flat EUR/day.
- Hrvelec quoted 32.5-34.0 at 35 d vs 31.5-32.0 at 42 d; 42 d costs us EUR 1.4k (0.017).
- D02 C1 deals: 0.383 at 42 d vs 0.276 at 35 d. lead_cap leaves this on the table.
6) After a final offer: a timeout kills the thread 77/81, a no-sheet message keeps it alive 29/29, mirroring its alternative is agreed 156/156. A9h has rfq_hold=False.
7) Payment: C_best always uses an EXTREME payment option (fastest if the supplier's rate > 8 %, else 90). Misses: P04 pay 60 in 14/20 deals = -0.047 each; P02 clause deals at 60. Your payrate variant is the right fix; make sure it picks extremes.
8) Contract length is priced at 0 by the bots (8/8 alternatives). Deadband 0->5 % is a wash at their prices. Stabilise cases: the true supplier is should-cost/1.02 with cash 9-9.6 % (family) or 6.1-6.6 % (group), fitted to the cent on P01/P02/P03/D01.

PROPOSED SPLIT (all flagged, defaults untouched):
- ME:
  (A) escalation collection: on approval/management cues, never accept that turn; send one more message to collect the approved step.
  (C) RFQ unlock protocol: never close while an unlocked supplier owes its rest; ask at target in the rest round; re-cite a fresh rival >= 10 % below to bidders not yet unlocked; plus rfq_hold keep-alive for final-offer threads.
  (D) lead-slack rule in place of lead_cap, using the supplier's own %/day where it gives one.
- YOU:
  (B) R1 fact selection: the best-landing facts in the FIRST mail, i.e. falling indices of drivers the supplier itself names in its opening ("X rose ... and is N % of our cost"), ranked by share x fall, never rising drivers or own POs. P08: the PPI fall in R1.
  Plus payrate with extremes.
- You know the fact planner and the planner's P18 front-load lesson (0.401) better than I do.

Does that split work? I'm starting (A) now in my gap worktree (on 44dcc24) and will send the commit with unit tests.

import json, re, collections
d = json.load(open('sessions_full.json'))
cue = re.compile(r"approv|management|committee|internally|Geschäftsleitung|Freigabe", re.I)
texts = collections.Counter(); status = collections.Counter(); delays = collections.Counter()
ex = []
for sid, s in d.items():
    tr = (s.get('result') or {}).get('trace') or []
    for i, m in enumerate(tr):
        mv = m.get('move') or {}
        if not (m.get('actor') or '').startswith('sup:'): continue
        body = mv.get('text') or ''
        reasons = ' '.join(m.get('reasons') or [])
        hits = [x for x in re.split(r'(?<=[.!?])\s+', body + ' ' + reasons) if cue.search(x)]
        if hits:
            for h in hits: texts[h.strip()[:110]] += 1
            status[mv.get('status')] += 1
            delays[(mv.get('signals') or {}).get('reply_delay_days')] += 1
            if len(ex) < 6 and s.get('set') == 'practice':
                ex.append((sid, s.get('case_id'), m.get('round'), mv.get('status'), hits[:2]))
print('status at cue:', dict(status)); print('reply_delay_days at cue:', dict(delays))
for t, n in texts.most_common(30): print(f'{n:5d}  {t}')
print(); [print(e) for e in ex]
EOF

"""A clause package in a supplier-health case goes out at the payment term and price cheapest for us (variant
A9h-clausepay). P02: Nordmark agreed at once to every clause package we sent, all at 60 days at the round's goal."""

import json
from pathlib import Path

from arena_kit import complete_offer, total_cost
from proto.engine import Thread
from proto.practice import PracticeNegotiator
from proto.variants import VARIANTS

CASE = json.loads((Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "cases" / "P02.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
SUP = CASE["suppliers"][0]
OPEN = {"unit_price": 370.96, "payment_days": 30, "index_clause": None}


def packages(variant, goal):
    n = PracticeNegotiator.__new__(PracticeNegotiator)
    n.c, n.case_id, n.cfg, n.quiet, n.log = None, "case:P02", VARIANTS[variant][1], True, []
    n.sid, n.case, n.b, n.deadline, n.slowest = "t", CASE, CASE["buyer"], None, 0
    t = Thread(SUP, [{"from": f"sales@{SUP}", "status": "open", "body": "Our offer.", "attachments": [],
                      "term_sheets": [{"term_sheet_id": "offer:x-0", "terms": dict(OPEN)}]}])
    t.std = {k: v for k, v in complete_offer(CASE, OPEN).items() if k != "unit_price"}
    n.threads, n.alt, n.c_alt, n.relationship = {SUP: t}, {}, float("inf"), True
    n.c_open = total_cost(CASE, complete_offer(CASE, OPEN), t.std, None)
    n._estimate()
    return n, t, n.meso(t, goal)


def test_the_clause_package_moves_to_its_cheapest_payment_term_and_price():
    goal = 2_246_000
    _, _, frozen = packages("A9h-frozen", goal)
    n, t, plan = packages("A9h-clausepay", goal)
    old = [p for p in frozen if p.get("index_clause")]
    new = [p for p in plan if p.get("index_clause")]
    assert old and new
    assert new[0]["payment_days"] == 90 and old[0]["payment_days"] == 60
    assert n.C(t, complete_offer(CASE, new[0])) < n.C(t, complete_offer(CASE, old[0]))
    assert [p for p in plan if not p.get("index_clause")] == [p for p in frozen if not p.get("index_clause")]


def test_no_change_outside_supplier_health_cases():
    cfg = VARIANTS["A9h-clausepay"][1]
    assert cfg.clause_pay_best and not VARIANTS["A9h-frozen"][1].clause_pay_best

"""RFQ fact allocation: a shared fact goes to the leading supplier only, and never twice (one claim per case)."""

from dataclasses import replace

from test_engine_clock import C1, J1, Arena

import proto.engine as eng
from proto.variants import VARIANTS


def test_shared_facts_go_to_the_leader_once_and_own_facts_to_their_owner():
    n = eng.Negotiator(Arena(), "case:D02", replace(VARIANTS["A9hr"][1], pushes=0, rfq_pushes=0), quiet=True)
    lead, other = n.threads[C1], n.threads[J1]  # C1's opening (EUR 16.00) is the best standing offer
    assert n.best_standing()[1] is lead
    facts = [("cost:part:SH-220", "should-cost"), (["idx:A@1", "idx:A@2"], "index"), (f"sc:{J1[4:]}@2026Q3", "J1 card")]
    assert n.pick_facts(other, facts, 2) == [(f"sc:{J1[4:]}@2026Q3", "J1 card")]  # not the leader: only its own
    assert n.pick_facts(lead, facts, 2) == facts[:2]  # the leader gets the shared facts
    assert n.pick_facts(lead, facts, 2) == []  # and never the same ones again
    assert n.pick_facts(other, facts, 2) == []  # spent for the case, and the card is not its own

# How the supplier bots decide (research, night of 10-11 Oct)

Six analysis tracks over **all 1,572 sessions on our key** (309 practice, 1,263 sandbox; traces, supplier reasons,
back offices), the case files and the arena's cost formula. Four tracks finished their checks; the rest is marked.
Numbers are from code on the dump (`/v1/sessions` + `/v1/sessions/{sid}` + back office, free GETs).

## The opponent, as far as we can tell
1. **The numbers come from rules over our term sheets; the LLM writes the e-mail.** Same history of term sheets,
   fresh replies: identical terms in 77-83 % of pairs even when our text differed; identical status in 98-99.9 %.
   Our wording is a small lever (style search 0.699-0.721; writer tests: parity).
2. **Round 1 is a recomputation that sets most of the case.** The first counter delivers 64-100 % of everything a
   supplier ever concedes (P08 64 %, P18 46 % of the room, P03/P04/P10 ~100 %). It hardly follows our ask: P08
   answers 5.45-5.52 whether we ask 5.06 or 5.43. An ask far beyond the room hardens it (probes: P08 asked 5.00 ->
   5.72; P18 asked 4.95 -> 5.60).
3. **Each persona goes final at a fixed round**: P10 R1 (24/30), P18 R3 (30/31), P04 R3, P07 and P11 R4, P08 R3-5.
   In between it is reciprocal: our move + a new fact that lands -> counter 85 %, 1.97 % mean; a move without a
   fact 0.33 %; neither -> hold 69 %. Some personas price on a grid (P05, P11 EUR 0.50; P18, P10, P01 EUR 0.10).
4. **The endpoint is a plateau far above the floor.** In floor-bound cases (leverage, routine, quality, capacity,
   RFQ) suppliers stop 4-15 % above the price that C_best implies (P10 +15 %, P18 +14-15 %, P05 +10 %, P07 +9 %,
   P08 +5-7 %, P11 +4 %). Records sit 1-4.5 % below our endpoints. In stabilise cases we already reach ~C_best.
5. **C_best is reproducible offline** (to EUR 0.01): min over supplier x lever options x price above a hidden floor
   of `total_cost`, relationship charge included. The arena's true supplier: full cost = its own should-cost / 1.02;
   cash rate ~9-9.6 % (family/founder) or 6.1-6.6 % (group); payment-only alternatives reveal it (P02 6.6 %).
6. **Two real "extra step" mechanisms, both visible in the e-mail:**
   - *Approval:* "Any further step needs approval from our management." With one more ask below its offer the next
     reply carried the approval 31 of 40 times (median -1.3 % of price, 0 walk-aways). We threw 39 away by
     accepting in that round (P02 6c1f4006871e6587: accepted at the band end, 0.157).
   - *Rival half step (RFQ):* a verified rival price >= ~5 % below its standing offer -> "We need to clarify this
     internally - we will come back to you on price" (half step, ~11-14 % of C), the rest on its next reply. Once
     per supplier; owner-run suppliers fire in R1 (J1, Dralveck), export managers rarely (Hrvelec never).
7. **Final offers:** a timeout after a final offer ends the thread 77/81; a message without a term sheet keeps it
   alive 29/29; mirroring its own alternative is agreed 156/156; a lower ask on the same package gained 0 of 53
   practice pushes and lost 2 suppliers (decision 0008 stands).
8. **Levers:** contract length is worth 0 to the bots (8/8 alternatives); the deadband is a wash; C_best always
   uses an extreme payment term (fastest if the supplier's cash rate > our 8 %, else 90 days); long-lead suppliers
   charge ~0.5 % of price per day of acceleration while our late cost is flat (P10: 42 vs 54 days = +EUR 1.9/unit).

## What we tested tonight (AI brain, fresh replies)
| Idea | Result |
|---|---|
| First ask -6 % (`knob-anchor6`) | 0.672, **but it changed round 1 in only 3 of 10 cases** |
| Six holds / linear curve | 0.701 / P02 0.46 |
| Fact planner + RFQ rival loop | 0.715 (= A9h) |
| Firm far ask + management request + 36-month "volume" framing (probes P08, P18) | both hardened, both withdrew after a push: no deal |
| Landing facts first (`A9h-landing`) | P08 0.560, P18 0.497: no gain |
| Cash rate from payment alternatives (`A9h-payrate`) | inside the usual ranges: no gain |
| Clause package at its cheapest payment term (P02) | **0.735 x 5 vs 0.63-0.68: in the final build** |

## Caveats
- **The arena caches replies** keyed on the whole conversation: a byte-identical mail gets the stored reply in
  < 3 s. 13 % of practice sessions were replays (e.g. the 19:04 pass = the 18:49 pass). Guard: median reply >= 15 s.
- **The AI budget runs dry**: practice and sandbox fell back to a rule-based brain at ~23:45 and came back at
  ~00:00 (reset at midnight). Sunday morning may hit the fallback again. The final is never affected.

## Open
- `A9h-owed` (branch `gap`): collect an announced step instead of accepting; in RFQs never close while a bidder
  owes it; keep resting final-offer threads alive. Under test on sandbox D02.
- Nobody has found what gets records 1-4.5 % below our plateaus (P05 record 0.965 = EUR 26.67, ours 28.75-29.50).

2. **Round 1 is a recomputation that sets most of the case.** The first counter delivers 64-100 % of everything a
   supplier ever concedes (P08 64 %, P18 46 % of the room, P03/P04/P10 ~100 %). It hardly follows our ask: P08
   answers 5.45-5.52 whether we ask 5.06 or 5.43. An ask far beyond the room hardens it (probes: P08 asked 5.00 ->
   5.72; P18 asked 4.95 -> 5.60).
3. **Each persona goes final at a fixed round**: P10 R1 (24/30), P18 R3 (30/31), P04 R3, P07 and P11 R4, P08 R3-5.
   In between it is reciprocal: our move + a new fact that lands -> counter 85 %, 1.97 % mean; a move without a
   fact 0.33 %; neither -> hold 69 %. Some personas price on a grid (P05, P11 EUR 0.50; P18, P10, P01 EUR 0.10).
4. **The endpoint is a plateau far above the floor.** In floor-bound cases (leverage, routine, quality, capacity,
   RFQ) suppliers stop 4-15 % above the price that C_best implies (P10 +15 %, P18 +14-15 %, P05 +10 %, P07 +9 %,
   P08 +5-7 %, P11 +4 %). Records sit 1-4.5 % below our endpoints. In stabilise cases we already reach ~C_best.
5. **C_best is reproducible offline** (to EUR 0.01): min over supplier x lever options x price above a hidden floor
   of `total_cost`, relationship charge included. The arena's true supplier: full cost = its own should-cost / 1.02;
   cash rate ~9-9.6 % (family/founder) or 6.1-6.6 % (group); payment-only alternatives reveal it (P02 6.6 %).
6. **Two real "extra step" mechanisms, both visible in the e-mail:**
   - *Approval:* "Any further step needs approval from our management." With one more ask below its offer the next
     reply carried the approval 31 of 40 times (median -1.3 % of price, 0 walk-aways). We threw 39 away by
     accepting in that round (P02 6c1f4006871e6587: accepted at the band end, 0.157).
   - *Rival half step (RFQ):* a verified rival price >= ~5 % below its standing offer -> "We need to clarify this
     internally - we will come back to you on price" (half step, ~11-14 % of C), the rest on its next reply. Once
     per supplier; owner-run suppliers fire in R1 (J1, Dralveck), export managers rarely (Hrvelec never).
7. **Final offers:** a timeout after a final offer ends the thread 77/81; a message without a term sheet keeps it
   alive 29/29; mirroring its own alternative is agreed 156/156; a lower ask on the same package gained 0 of 53
   practice pushes and lost 2 suppliers (decision 0008 stands).
8. **Levers:** contract length is worth 0 to the bots (8/8 alternatives); the deadband is a wash; C_best always
   uses an extreme payment term (fastest if the supplier's cash rate > our 8 %, else 90 days); long-lead suppliers
   charge ~0.5 % of price per day of acceleration while our late cost is flat (P10: 42 vs 54 days = +EUR 1.9/unit).

| Idea | Result |
|---|---|
| First ask -6 % (`knob-anchor6`) | 0.672, **but it changed round 1 in only 3 of 10 cases** |
| Six holds / linear curve | 0.701 / P02 0.46 |
| Fact planner + RFQ rival loop | 0.715 (= A9h) |
| Firm far ask + management request + 36-month "volume" framing (probes P08, P18) | both hardened, both withdrew after a push: no deal |
| Landing facts first (`A9h-landing`) | P08 0.560, P18 0.497: no gain |
| Cash rate from payment alternatives (`A9h-payrate`) | inside the usual ranges: no gain |
| Clause package at its cheapest payment term (P02) | **0.735 x 5 vs 0.63-0.68: in the final build** |

## Caveats
- **The arena caches replies** keyed on the whole conversation: a byte-identical mail gets the stored reply in
  < 3 s. 13 % of practice sessions were replays (e.g. the 19:04 pass = the 18:49 pass). Guard: median reply >= 15 s.
- **The AI budget runs dry**: practice and sandbox fell back to a rule-based brain at ~23:45 and came back at
  ~00:00 (reset at midnight). Sunday morning may hit the fallback again. The final is never affected.

  owes it; keep resting final-offer threads alive. Under test on sandbox D02.

def meso(self, t, c_goal):
        """Up to meso_n packages that each cost us c_goal, differing in the levers the supplier may value."""
        if self.cfg.price_freeze and FREEZE.search(t.last.get("body") or "") and (fp := self.frozen_packages(t)):
            return fp
        # "equal cost to us" must be tight where the room is small (P02: 1 % of C was more than the whole room)
        room = max(self.c_open - self.target_c, 0.0) if self.c_open < float("inf") else 0.01 * c_goal
        tol = max(min(0.002 * c_goal, 0.1 * room), 0.0005 * c_goal)
        offered = t.sheets[0]["terms"] if t.sheets else {}
        grid = [g for g in lever_grid(self.case, {**t.std, **offered}) if must_haves_ok(self.case, g, t.std)]
        if self.cfg.lead_cap and "lead_time_days" in self.case["negotiable"]:
            # never beyond our need: a longer lead time costs us late days and suppliers rarely pay for it (P10)
            need = self.b.get("need_lead_time_days")
            grid = [g for g in grid if g.get("lead_time_days") is None or g["lead_time_days"] <= need] or grid
        if self.cfg.meet_cheapest:
            # a term the supplier explicitly insists on becomes a condition of EVERY package, in the variant of that
        for g in grid:
            p = price_for_c(self.case, g, t.std, c_goal, t.est if self.relationship else None)
            terms = complete_offer(self.case, {**g, "unit_price": p})
            c = self.C(t, terms)
            if p <= 0.5 or (abs(c - c_goal) > max(tol, 0.01 * c_goal) and c < c_goal):
                continue
            # guard (teammates' P02 zero): never offer a higher price than the supplier itself asks - cap at its price
            # (still a better package for us: P10) - and never a package that costs us more than its standing offer
            capped = False
            if their_price is not None and p > their_price:
                terms = complete_offer(self.case, {**g, "unit_price": their_price})
                p, c, capped = their_price, self.C(t, terms), True
            if c >= their_c:
                continue
            near = sum(terms.get(k) != offered.get(k) for k in terms if k != "unit_price" and k in offered)
            terms["_capped"] = capped
            sv = supplier_value(self.case, {k: v for k, v in terms.items() if k != "_capped"}, t.est)
            if self.cfg.penalty_aversion:  # suppliers price penalty clauses far above their expected cost (P11)
                sv -= self.cfg.penalty_aversion * (terms.get("chargeback_eur_per_complaint") or 0) * (terms.get("ppm_commitment") or 0) / 1e6
            priced.append((sv, near, terms, c))
        everything = list(priced)
        hits = [x for x in priced if abs(x[3] - c_goal) <= tol or x[2].get("_capped")]
        # full coverage first (P10): a package covering the whole need over the horizon beats a partial one
        def full(x):
            tt = x[2]
            vol_ok = (tt.get("volume_per_year") or self.b["need_per_year"]) >= self.b["need_per_year"]
            months = tt.get("contract_months", self.case.get("fixed_terms", {}).get("contract_months"))
            return vol_ok and (months is None or months >= 12 * self.b["horizon_years"])
        if any(full(x) for x in hits):
            hits = [x for x in hits if full(x)]
        if not hits and priced:
            # the goal is out of reach (e.g. below what the supplier-health term allows): offer the
            # packages closest to it, i.e. the cheapest ones for us, each at its cheapest price
            lowest = min(x[3] for x in priced)
            hits = [x for x in priced if x[3] <= lowest * 1.005]
        priced = [(x[0], x[1], {k: v for k, v in x[2].items() if k != "_capped"}) for x in hits]
        everything = [(x[0], x[1], {k: v for k, v in x[2].items() if k != "_capped"}, x[3]) for x in everything]
        if not priced:
            return []
        if self.cfg.pick == "near":
            priced.sort(key=lambda x: (x[1], -x[0]))

def test_the_rival_trigger_cites_the_cheapest_price_well_below_its_own_and_never_a_dearer_one():
    from test_engine_clock import Arena

    n = eng.Negotiator(Arena(), "case:D02", replace(VARIANTS["A9h-rival"][1], pushes=0, rfq_pushes=0), quiet=True)
    j1, c1 = n.threads[J1], n.threads[C1]  # J1 opens at 17.10 FCA; C1 at 16.00 EXW with a 45-day lead (not compliant)
    pick = n.rival_cheaper(j1)
    assert pick and pick[0] == f"offer:{C1}-0"  # 6.4 % below: cited although its package misses our must-haves
    assert n.rival_cheaper(c1) is None  # J1's 17.10 is dearer than C1's own price: telling C1 so helps nobody
    j1.events.append({"from": "buyer", "refs": [f"offer:{C1}-0"], "term_sheets": []})
    assert n.rival_cheaper(j1) is None  # never the same offer twice (a duplicate)
    n.cfg = replace(n.cfg, rival_gap=0.10)
    j1.events.pop()
    assert n.rival_cheaper(j1) is None  # 6.4 % is below a 10 % bar
EOF
uv run pytest tests/test_engine_owed.py -q 2>&1 | tail -3; uv run ruff check proto/engine.py proto/variants.py tests/test_engine_owed.py proto/probe.py 2>&1 | tail -5

input.message:
RESEARCH (03:00): a second candidate is on branch gap: 614eea6 Variant A9h-rival = A9h-owed + rival_gap 0.05. Full suite 130 passed / 3 skipped; ruff clean.

WHY: the D02 logs of my A9h-owed sandbox runs show that A9h wastes the RFQ rival trigger. Owner-type suppliers give a half step when shown a rival PRICE >= 5 % below their own: J1 100 % at 5-20 %, Dralveck 100 % at 5-10 %; they check only the cited offer's price. In all 3 D02 runs:
- The stagger lead J1 (17.10) got its first mail with NO rival. C1's 16.00 opening (6.4 % below) was excluded because its 45-day lead breaks our must-have, and others are picked by our C among compliant sheets only.
- Later J1, already at 15.00, was shown C1's 15.80, i.e. "you're already the cheapest". The same offer was cited twice, so a duplicate.
- Result: no half step for J1 in any run; deals 0.661-0.682 at J1 13.8-13.9. In older sandbox runs J1 threads WITH a half step reached 0.67-0.74 vs 0.43-0.61 without, at the same ask depth.

FIX (Config.rival_gap): from the first mail, cite the lowest-PRICED rival offer (any package) not yet shown to that supplier, only if >= 5 % below its own price; never a dearer one, never twice. The announced rest is collected by A9h-owed's never-close-while-owed rule.

P05 IMPACT (practice): Hrvelec's 31.5 opening (52-day lead, non-compliant) is currently never cited.
- Under A9h-rival it goes to Dralveck (36.0: 12.5 % below) in R1, and the lowest unseen price goes to Fuchsreiter (38.5: 18-21 % below). Fuchsreiter fired only 5/28 under A9h's small gaps.
- Expect both owners' half steps in R1. The endpoint may still sit ~29.5, but competition gets earlier and stronger.

Suggestion for your practice batch: A9h-rival instead of (or alongside) A9h-owed on P05 x2; it includes owed. P02 isn't an RFQ, so A9h-owed covers it.
I'm running A9h-rival on sandbox D02 x6 (3 at a time) as soon as my last 3 A9h-owed D02 runs finish (~03:05), and will send you the paired numbers.

do sleep 15; done; python3 - <<'EOF'
import json, re, statistics as S
rows = [json.loads(l) for l in open('logs/events.jsonl') if l.strip()]
for sess in ['4585a144d5d71d74', 'dc555baf2e7b2df2']:
    path = [f"{r.get('supplier')[-3:]}:{(r.get('terms') or {}).get('unit_price')}{'*' if re.search('clarif', r.get('body') or '', re.I) else ''}{(r.get('status') or '?')[0]}" for r in rows if r.get('session') == sess and r.get('kind') == 'supplier']
    res = [r for r in rows if r.get('session') == sess and r.get('kind') == 'result'][0]
    took = [r.get('took') for r in rows if r.get('session') == sess and r.get('kind') == 'supplier' and isinstance(r.get('took'), (int, float)) and r.get('took') > 0]
    t = res.get('terms') or {}
    print(sess, 'score', round(res.get('score') or 0, 3), res.get('supplier'), t.get('unit_price'), 'pay', t.get('payment_days'), 'lead', t.get('lead_time_days'), '| median reply', round(S.median(took), 1) if took else None)
    print('   ', ' > '.join(path))
EOF
date '+%H:%M'

p = 'proto/engine.py'
s = open(p).read()
# config field
old = "    rival_gap: float = 0.0\n"
assert s.count(old) == 1
s = s.replace(old, old + """    # While collecting an announced step, keep our previous ask instead of moving up the curve: the step comes anyway
    # (a rival rest even after a timeout), and a supplier agrees only at or above its own computed price, so a lower
    # ask never costs price. P05 03:08: our curve rose from 26.93 to 28.72 in Dralveck's rest round and it agreed at
    # 28.72; D02 rest rounds moved 7.9 % after asks 12 %+ below vs 4.9 % after 8-12 %.
    owed_hold: bool = False
""")
# helper
old = "    def rival_cheaper(self, t):"
s = s.replace(old, '''    def last_ask_c(self, t):
        """C of our cheapest term sheet in our last mail to t (None before our first)."""
        mine = [m for m in t.events if m.get("from") == "buyer" and m.get("term_sheets")]
        cs = [self.C(t, complete_offer(self.case, s2["terms"])) for s2 in (mine[-1]["term_sheets"] if mine else [])
              if (s2.get("terms") or {}).get("unit_price")]
        return min(cs) if cs else None

''' + old, 1)
# rfq branch
old = """                    goal = min(goal, min(own) * (1 - cfg.owed_gap))  # below its offer (deeper if our curve already is)
                t.collected = 1"""
assert s.count(old) == 1
s = s.replace(old, """                    goal = min(goal, min(own) * (1 - cfg.owed_gap))  # below its offer (deeper if our curve already is)
                if cfg.owed_hold and (prev := self.last_ask_c(t)):
                    goal = min(goal, prev)  # no concession while it owes us a step
                t.collected = 1""")
# single branch
old = """                    owed_cap = c * (1 - cfg.owed_gap)
                    goal = min(goal, owed_cap)"""
assert s.count(old) == 1
s = s.replace(old, """                    owed_cap = c * (1 - cfg.owed_gap)
                    if cfg.owed_hold and (prev := self.last_ask_c(t)):
                        owed_cap = min(owed_cap, prev)  # no concession while it owes us a step
                    goal = min(goal, owed_cap)""")
open(p, 'w').write(s)
print('ok')

import json, re, statistics as S
rows = [json.loads(l) for l in open('logs/events.jsonl') if l.strip()]
res = [r for r in rows if r.get('kind') == 'result']
for r in res[-4:]:
    sess = r.get('session')
    path = [f"{(x.get('supplier') or '')[-3:]}:{(x.get('terms') or {}).get('unit_price')}{'*' if re.search('clarif', x.get('body') or '', re.I) else ''}{(x.get('status') or '?')[0]}" for x in rows if x.get('session') == sess and x.get('kind') == 'supplier']
    took = [x.get('took') for x in rows if x.get('session') == sess and x.get('kind') == 'supplier' and isinstance(x.get('took'), (int, float)) and x.get('took') > 0]
    t = r.get('terms') or {}
    print(r.get('case'), sess, 'score', round(r.get('score') or 0, 3), r.get('supplier'), t.get('unit_price'), '| median reply', round(S.median(took), 1) if took else None)
    print('   ', ' > '.join(path))
EOF
date '+%H:%M'

# How the supplier bots decide (research, night of 10-11 Oct)

Six analysis tracks over **all 1,572 sessions on our key** (309 practice, 1,263 sandbox; traces, supplier reasons,
back offices), the case files and the arena's cost formula. Four tracks finished their checks; the rest is marked.
Numbers are from code on the dump (`/v1/sessions` + `/v1/sessions/{sid}` + back office, free GETs).

## The opponent, as far as we can tell
1. **The numbers come from rules over our term sheets; the LLM writes the e-mail.** Same history of term sheets,
   fresh replies: identical terms in 77-83 % of pairs even when our text differed; identical status in 98-99.9 %.
   Our wording is a small lever (style search 0.699-0.721; writer tests: parity).
2. **Round 1 is a recomputation that sets most of the case.** The first counter delivers 64-100 % of everything a
   supplier ever concedes (P08 64 %, P18 46 % of the room, P03/P04/P10 ~100 %). It hardly follows our ask: P08
   answers 5.45-5.52 whether we ask 5.06 or 5.43. An ask far beyond the room hardens it (probes: P08 asked 5.00 ->
   5.72; P18 asked 4.95 -> 5.60).
3. **Each persona goes final at a fixed round**: P10 R1 (24/30), P18 R3 (30/31), P04 R3, P07 and P11 R4, P08 R3-5.
   In between it is reciprocal: our move + a new fact that lands -> counter 85 %, 1.97 % mean; a move without a
   fact 0.33 %; neither -> hold 69 %. Some personas price on a grid (P05, P11 EUR 0.50; P18, P10, P01 EUR 0.10).
4. **The endpoint is a plateau far above the floor.** In floor-bound cases (leverage, routine, quality, capacity,
   RFQ) suppliers stop 4-15 % above the price that C_best implies (P10 +15 %, P18 +14-15 %, P05 +10 %, P07 +9 %,
   P08 +5-7 %, P11 +4 %). Records sit 1-4.5 % below our endpoints. In stabilise cases we already reach ~C_best.
5. **C_best is reproducible offline** (to EUR 0.01): min over supplier x lever options x price above a hidden floor
   of `total_cost`, relationship charge included. The arena's true supplier: full cost = its own should-cost / 1.02;
   cash rate ~9-9.6 % (family/founder) or 6.1-6.6 % (group); payment-only alternatives reveal it (P02 6.6 %).
6. **Two real "extra step" mechanisms, both visible in the e-mail:**
   - *Approval:* "Any further step needs approval from our management." With one more ask below its offer the next
     reply carried the approval 31 of 40 times (median -1.3 % of price, 0 walk-aways). We threw 39 away by
     accepting in that round (P02 6c1f4006871e6587: accepted at the band end, 0.157).
   - *Rival half step (RFQ):* a verified rival price >= ~5 % below its standing offer -> "We need to clarify this
     internally - we will come back to you on price" (half step, ~11-14 % of C), the rest on its next reply. Once
     per supplier; owner-run suppliers fire in R1 (J1, Dralveck), export managers rarely (Hrvelec never).
7. **Final offers:** a timeout after a final offer ends the thread 77/81; a message without a term sheet keeps it
   alive 29/29; mirroring its own alternative is agreed 156/156; a lower ask on the same package gained 0 of 53
   practice pushes and lost 2 suppliers (decision 0008 stands).
8. **Levers:** contract length is worth 0 to the bots (8/8 alternatives); the deadband is a wash; C_best always
   uses an extreme payment term (fastest if the supplier's cash rate > our 8 %, else 90 days); long-lead suppliers
   charge ~0.5 % of price per day of acceleration while our late cost is flat (P10: 42 vs 54 days = +EUR 1.9/unit).

## What we tested tonight (AI brain, fresh replies)
| Idea | Result |
|---|---|
| First ask -6 % (`knob-anchor6`) | 0.672, **but it changed round 1 in only 3 of 10 cases** |
| Six holds / linear curve | 0.701 / P02 0.46 |
| Fact planner + RFQ rival loop | 0.715 (= A9h) |
| Firm far ask + management request + 36-month "volume" framing (probes P08, P18) | both hardened, both withdrew after a push: no deal |
| Landing facts first (`A9h-landing`) | P08 0.560, P18 0.497: no gain |
| Cash rate from payment alternatives (`A9h-payrate`) | inside the usual ranges: no gain |
| Clause package at its cheapest payment term (P02) | **0.735 x 5 vs 0.63-0.68: in the final build** |

## Caveats
- **The arena caches replies** keyed on the whole conversation: a byte-identical mail gets the stored reply in
  < 3 s. 13 % of practice sessions were replays (e.g. the 19:04 pass = the 18:49 pass). Guard: median reply >= 15 s.
- **The AI budget runs dry**: practice and sandbox fell back to a rule-based brain at ~23:45 and came back at
  ~00:00 (reset at midnight). Sunday morning may hit the fallback again. The final is never affected.

## Open
- `A9h-owed` (branch `gap`): collect an announced step instead of accepting; in RFQs never close while a bidder
  owes it; keep resting final-offer threads alive. Under test on sandbox D02.
- Nobody has found what gets records 1-4.5 % below our plateaus (P05 record 0.965 = EUR 26.67, ours 28.75-29.50).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Play against arena-sim on this machine: no key, no quota, no real suppliers.
# Loads every saved case file (starter-kit/cases: P01-P19, D01, D02) next to the sim's own S01-S03.
#
#   scripts/sim.sh play case:P01 --agent llm -v      # any arena command, pointed at the sim
#   scripts/sim.sh run --set practice --agent llm    # all cases in parallel
#   SIM_CLOCK=0 scripts/sim.sh play case:P05 -v      # without the 60-second rule
#   scripts/sim.sh stop
set -euo pipefail
KIT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../starter-kit" && pwd)"
PORT="${SIM_PORT:-8000}"
export ARENA_URL="http://127.0.0.1:$PORT"
cd "$KIT"

if [[ "${1:-}" == "stop" ]]; then
  pkill -f "arena-sim serve.*--port $PORT" && echo "arena-sim stopped" || echo "arena-sim was not running"
  exit 0
fi

if ! curl -sf "$ARENA_URL/health" > /dev/null; then
  mkdir -p ../logs
  clock=(); [[ "${SIM_CLOCK:-1}" == "0" ]] && clock=(--no-clock)
  nohup uv run arena-sim serve --port "$PORT" --data data/package --cases cases ${clock[@]+"${clock[@]}"} \
    > ../logs/sim.log 2>&1 &
  for _ in $(seq 30); do curl -sf "$ARENA_URL/health" > /dev/null && break; sleep 0.5; done
  echo "arena-sim started on $ARENA_URL (log: logs/sim.log)"
fi

# A fresh simulator key per call: the sim's own quota never runs out, and the real key is never used.
ARENA_API_KEY="$(uv run arena register "sim-$(whoami)-$$" sim | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.loads(sys.stdin.read().split("\n\n")[0])["api_key"])')"
export ARENA_API_KEY
[[ $# -gt 0 ]] && exec uv run arena "$@"

#   scripts/sim.sh play case:P01 --agent llm -v      # any arena command, pointed at the sim
#   scripts/sim.sh run --set practice --agent llm    # all cases in parallel
#   SIM_CLOCK=0 scripts/sim.sh play case:P05 -v      # without the 60-second rule
#   scripts/sim.sh stop
set -euo pipefail
KIT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../starter-kit" && pwd)"
PORT="${SIM_PORT:-8000}"
export ARENA_URL="http://127.0.0.1:$PORT"
cd "$KIT"

if [[ "${1:-}" == "stop" ]]; then
  pkill -f "arena-sim serve.*--port $PORT" && echo "arena-sim stopped" || echo "arena-sim was not running"
  exit 0
fi

if ! curl -sf "$ARENA_URL/health" > /dev/null; then
  mkdir -p ../logs
  clock=(); [[ "${SIM_CLOCK:-1}" == "0" ]] && clock=(--no-clock)
  nohup uv run arena-sim serve --port "$PORT" --data data/package --cases cases ${clock[@]+"${clock[@]}"} \
    > ../logs/sim.log 2>&1 &
  for _ in $(seq 30); do curl -sf "$ARENA_URL/health" > /dev/null && break; sleep 0.5; done
  echo "arena-sim started on $ARENA_URL (log: logs/sim.log)"
fi

# A fresh simulator key per call: the sim's own quota never runs out, and the real key is never used.
ARENA_API_KEY="$(uv run arena register "sim-$(whoami)-$$" sim | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.loads(sys.stdin.read().split("\n\n")[0])["api_key"])')"
export ARENA_API_KEY
[[ $# -gt 0 ]] && exec uv run arena "$@"

     - "we have time, api credit and session. We can try... Collaborate with MAIN. Brainstorm solutions. Do whatever it takes." Ultracode was opted in for that turn.

   - **Constraints, preserve:**
     - Secrets only in root `.env`; never commit or print them (CLAUDE.md).
     - The agent must not read `/v1/events`, `/screen`, `/leaderboard`, `/results` during the final.

# How the supplier bots decide (research, night of 10-11 Oct)

Six analysis tracks over **all 1,572 sessions on our key** (309 practice, 1,263 sandbox; traces, supplier reasons,
back offices), the case files and the arena's cost formula. Four tracks finished their checks; the rest is marked.
Numbers are from code on the dump (`/v1/sessions` + `/v1/sessions/{sid}` + back office, free GETs).

## The opponent, as far as we can tell
1. **The numbers come from rules over our term sheets; the LLM writes the e-mail.** Same history of term sheets,
   fresh replies: identical terms in 77-83 % of pairs even when our text differed; identical status in 98-99.9 %.
   Our wording is a small lever (style search 0.699-0.721; writer tests: parity).
2. **Round 1 is a recomputation that sets most of the case.** The first counter delivers 64-100 % of everything a
   supplier ever concedes (P08 64 %, P18 46 % of the room, P03/P04/P10 ~100 %). It hardly follows our ask: P08
   answers 5.45-5.52 whether we ask 5.06 or 5.43. An ask far beyond the room hardens it (probes: P08 asked 5.00 ->
   5.72; P18 asked 4.95 -> 5.60).
3. **Each persona goes final at a fixed round**: P10 R1 (24/30), P18 R3 (30/31), P04 R3, P07 and P11 R4, P08 R3-5.
   In between it is reciprocal: our move + a new fact that lands -> counter 85 %, 1.97 % mean; a move without a
   fact 0.33 %; neither -> hold 69 %. Some personas price on a grid (P05, P11 EUR 0.50; P18, P10, P01 EUR 0.10).
4. **The endpoint is a plateau far above the floor.** In floor-bound cases (leverage, routine, quality, capacity,
   RFQ) suppliers stop 4-15 % above the price that C_best implies (P10 +15 %, P18 +14-15 %, P05 +10 %, P07 +9 %,
   P08 +5-7 %, P11 +4 %). Records sit 1-4.5 % below our endpoints. In stabilise cases we already reach ~C_best.
5. **C_best is reproducible offline** (to EUR 0.01): min over supplier x lever options x price above a hidden floor
   of `total_cost`, relationship charge included. The arena's true supplier: full cost = its own should-cost / 1.02;
   cash rate ~9-9.6 % (family/founder) or 6.1-6.6 % (group); payment-only alternatives reveal it (P02 6.6 %).
6. **Two real "extra step" mechanisms, both visible in the e-mail:**
   - *Approval:* "Any further step needs approval from our management." With one more ask below its offer the next
     reply carried the approval 31 of 40 times (median -1.3 % of price, 0 walk-aways). We threw 39 away by
     accepting in that round (P02 6c1f4006871e6587: accepted at the band end, 0.157).
   - *Rival half step (RFQ):* a verified rival price >= ~5 % below its standing offer -> "We need to clarify this
     internally - we will come back to you on price" (half step, ~11-14 % of C), the rest on its next reply. Once
     per supplier; owner-run suppliers fire in R1 (J1, Dralveck), export managers rarely (Hrvelec never).
7. **Final offers:** a timeout after a final offer ends the thread 77/81; a message without a term sheet keeps it
   alive 29/29; mirroring its own alternative is agreed 156/156; a lower ask on the same package gained 0 of 53
   practice pushes and lost 2 suppliers (decision 0008 stands).
8. **Levers:** contract length is worth 0 to the bots (8/8 alternatives); the deadband is a wash; C_best always
   uses an extreme payment term (fastest if the supplier's cash rate > our 8 %, else 90 days); long-lead suppliers
   charge ~0.5 % of price per day of acceleration while our late cost is flat (P10: 42 vs 54 days = +EUR 1.9/unit).

## What we tested tonight (AI brain, fresh replies)
| Idea | Result |
|---|---|
| First ask -6 % (`knob-anchor6`) | 0.672, **but it changed round 1 in only 3 of 10 cases** |
| Six holds / linear curve | 0.701 / P02 0.46 |
| Fact planner + RFQ rival loop | 0.715 (= A9h) |
| Firm far ask + management request + 36-month "volume" framing (probes P08, P18) | both hardened, both withdrew after a push: no deal |
| Landing facts first (`A9h-landing`) | P08 0.560, P18 0.497: no gain |
| Cash rate from payment alternatives (`A9h-payrate`) | inside the usual ranges: no gain |
| Clause package at its cheapest payment term (P02) | **0.735 x 5 vs 0.63-0.68: in the final build** |

## Caveats
- **The arena caches replies** keyed on the whole conversation: a byte-identical mail gets the stored reply in
  < 3 s. 13 % of practice sessions were replays (e.g. the 19:04 pass = the 18:49 pass). Guard: median reply >= 15 s.
- **The AI budget runs dry**: practice and sandbox fell back to a rule-based brain at ~23:45 and came back at
  ~00:00 (reset at midnight). Sunday morning may hit the fallback again. The final is never affected.

## RFQ: the rival trigger, used properly (Sunday 02:40-03:20, AI brain, fresh replies)
A9h wasted the rival trigger. It picked the rival by *our* C among must-have-compliant sheets, sent the stagger lead
none, and showed the leader dearer rivals (D02: J1 at 15.00 was shown C1's 15.80, twice). Three flags on branch
`gap`, all off in A9h:
- `collect_owed` (`A9h-owed`): never accept on a reply that announces a step ("needs approval from our
  management", "need to clarify this internally"); ask once more; in an RFQ never close while a bidder owes it.
  Alone it changed nothing measurable (MAIN's paired P05/P02 check): the step came anyway.
- `rival_gap` (`A9h-rival`): from the first mail, cite the lowest-priced rival offer (any package; the supplier
  checks only the price) not yet shown, if >= 5 % below the recipient's own price; never a dearer one.
- `owed_hold` (`A9h-rival-hold`): while a supplier owes its step, keep our previous ask. A supplier agrees only at or
  above its own computed price, so a lower ask never costs price, and the rest arrives anyway.

| | A9h | A9h-rival | A9h-rival-hold |
|---|---|---|---|
| P05 (practice) | 0.61-0.69 (best ever 0.736) | 0.739 x2 (28.72) | **0.814 x2 (28.00)** |
| D02 (sandbox) | 0.670 (n=6) | 0.724 x6 | **0.745, 0.766** |

P05 path with hold: Dralveck shown Hrvelec's 31.50 -> 36.00 to 30.50 "clarify internally" -> we keep 26.93 -> final
28.00; Fuchsreiter (fired 5/28 before) shown a price 18-21 % below -> 38.50 to 30.50 -> 29.00 -> 28.50. Sessions take
~3 min. Single-supplier cases are unchanged unless an approval cue appears.

## Open
- Adoption of `A9h-rival-hold` into the final build (MAIN's call, after its regression pass).
- Nobody has found what gets single-supplier records 1-4.5 % below our plateaus (P08, P18, P11, P07).
