Entire's CLI (`entire enable`) installs hooks that record Claude Code sessions and tie them to your git history. The search results come from different documentation versions, so the details vary somewhat.

**What `entire enable` does**
- Hooks are installed for your agent and for git. One source says the hooks capture session data at set points in your workflow, and that your commits stay clean because the metadata lives on a separate `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch. Enable Entire in Your Repository: entire enable. This installs agent and git hooks to work with your AI agent (Claude Code or Gemini CLI). The hooks capture session data at specific points in your workflow. Your code commits stay clean—all session metadata is stored on a separate entire/checkpoints/v1 branch.
- A third-party walkthrough says the command writes a `.claude/settings.json` file with hooks for session start and end, prompt submission, agent stops, and tool use, and adds a git post-commit hook that condenses session data on each commit. Running entire enable creates two things. First, it creates a .claude/settings.json file with hooks that tap into Claude Code's event system: SessionStart and SessionEnd capture when a session begins and ends; UserPromptSubmit captures every prompt you send. Because those hooks sit in the project's settings, they only track sessions launched from that directory. Because the hooks live in the project's .claude/settings.json, Entire tracks only the agent sessions launched from this directory.

**Checkpoints and strategies**
- The default strategy is manual-commit, which creates checkpoints when you or the agent commit. When checkpoints are created depends on your chosen strategy (default is manual-commit): Manual-commit: Checkpoints are created when you or the agent make a git commit. Auto-commit: Checkpoints are created after each agent response.
- Captured data includes the conversation transcript, changed files, tool calls, and token usage. Metadata Capture - Session data is on the entire/checkpoints/v1 branch. Captured Data: Entire captures the following from Claude Code sessions: Conversation, Full transcript of prompts and responses; File changes, All files modified during the session; Tool calls, Commands executed, files read, etc. Token usage, Input, output, and cache tokens

**Flags for `entire enable`** (per the Go package docs; availability depends on version)
- `--agent claude-code` selects the agent, and `--strategy auto-commit` switches strategies in older versions.
- `--force` reinstalls hooks, `--local` writes to `settings.local.json` (gitignored), and `--skip-push-sessions` turns off automatic session pushes.
- Newer releases add `--checkpoint-remote <provider:owner/repo>` to push checkpoint branches to a separate repo. entire explain Explain a session or commit is also listed in newer releases, along with other subcommands.

**Related commands**
- `entire status` shows the current session. `entire rewind` returns to an earlier checkpoint, and `entire resume` switches branches and restores checkpointed session metadata. entire resume Switch to a branch, restore latest checkpointed session metadata, and show command(s) to continue
- Rewind has limits. Rewind requires an active session with checkpoints. Check: entire status. If no session is active, checkpoints may only exist on the sessions branch.

**Caveats**
- Versions differ on the branch name. Older docs refer to `entire/sessions`, while newer ones use `entire/checkpoints/v1`.
- Some third-party reviewers say the rewind feature is more involved than the docs suggest, and that most agent integrations other than Claude Code are still in preview.
- Auto-summaries (`strategy_options.summarize.enabled`) need the Claude CLI installed and authenticated.

content.content:
**Install (from the README)**
- macOS/Linux, Homebrew: "brew install --cask entireio/tap/entire"
- macOS/Linux, script: "curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash"
- Windows, PowerShell: "irm https://entire.io/install.ps1 | iex"
- Windows, Scoop: "scoop install entire/entire"
- Go: "go install github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire@latest"

**Subcommands**
- Setup: enable, disable, status, agent, configure, doctor, clean, plugin
- Sessions and checkpoints: session, checkpoint, search, activity, recap, dispatch
- Account: login, logout, auth
- Control plane: cluster, org, project, repo, api
- Other: agent-help, labs, version
- Experimental (in `entire labs`): review, tokens, blame, why, experts, import, runner

**Checkpoint storage**
The README does not use a branch named `entire/checkpoints/v1`. Each checkpoint is its own git ref: "refs/entire/checkpoints/<shard>/<id>", where `<shard>` is the last two characters of the ID. Inspect them with `git for-each-ref refs/entire/checkpoints`.

**Pushing to origin**
There is no `entire push` command listed. Checkpoint data goes out with your own `git push`: the README says it "rides along with your own pushes," to one elected remote. `strategy_options.push_sessions` defaults to `true`, and `--skip-push-sessions` turns it off. The README does not say how this is implemented (for example, whether a pre-push hook is involved).

**Importing or attaching past sessions**
- `entire import` (experimental): "Import pre-existing agent history into Entire".
- `entire enable --import-history`: imports the selected agents' existing session history from the last 30 days during first-time setup.
- `entire session attach` and `entire session adopt` are listed, but the README gives no details on them.
- No `entire capture` command appears.

**Privacy**
- Transcripts are stored in your repository, so "If your repository is public, this data is visible to anyone."
- Secrets are redacted: "Entire automatically redacts detected secrets (API keys, tokens, credentials) from transcripts and metadata before writing a checkpoint, but redaction is best-effort."
- Opt-in PII redaction and scanner options are described in docs/security-and-privacy.md, which I did not have.
